Hardening pass from a Codex review, verified against the source before implementing. Each finding was reproduced (or refuted) first; two findings from the report were dropped or narrowed as wrong (see below). Every fix ships with a regression test, and where a bug was subtle the test was checked to fail against the pre-fix code.

## What's fixed (most user-visible first)

- **Renaming a cloud world silently disabled sync on your other devices.** `worlds.updatedAt` was both the metadata mtime *and* the save-revision cursor every device compares, so a rename bumped it, 409'd every other device's next push, and the 409 latched sync off for the session. Split into a dedicated monotonic `saveRevision` (migration `0004`).
- **Backgrounding on a phone switched off its own sync.** `pagehide` + `visibilitychange` both fire on mobile background, firing two pushes with the same base revision that conflicted with *each other*. Uploads now go through a latest-wins queue (one in flight, newest queued).
- **A brief network blip could kill a session that had already reconnected.** `onerror`+`onclose` both ran the close path; the second handshake's join kicked the first socket, whose stale close then tore down the live session. Fixed with a connection-generation guard.
- **A crashed game server lost session progress that involved no block edit.** Room persistence was gated on a dirty flag only five things set — inventory/health/XP/stats/etc. marked nothing. Occupied rooms now persist on the interval regardless, with a coalescing writer.
- **Server-authority hole:** any invited member could `PUT` an arbitrary `SaveData` over a multiplayer world's authoritative blob (`putSaveBlob` never checked `world.kind`). Now `sp-cloud`-only, mirroring `mintTicket`.
- **Malformed saves crashed the engine.** `parseSave` claimed to be total but only checked top-level array *types*, not entries; `{version:18,seed:1,changes:[1],players:[null]}` passed then threw in `GameEngine`. Now validates entries at the one shared seam; the cloud download (previously a bare cast) routes through it too.
- **Reconnecting a room mid-eviction** could resurrect it from stale state (dropped from the registry before its shutdown persisted). Eviction is now a windowless handoff.
- **Inbound frame reordering:** a text `tick` could apply while an earlier binary worldSync was still gunzipping, then be clobbered. Frames now apply in arrival order (text stays synchronous when nothing's pending).
- **World-creation input** was cast and trusted — `worldType`/`gameMode`/`difficulty` reached worldgen unvalidated, an out-of-range seed 500'd, and omitting `profileId` bypassed `MAX_WORLDS_PER_PROFILE`. All validated now; `mp` requires a profile.
- **Invite acceptance** wasn't transactional (a failed insert burned a use) and double-consumed under a same-user race; `resync` had no rate limit. Both fixed.
- **Docs + toolchain:** corrected five stale "client-only / localStorage / `Math.sin`" claims, and pinned Bun from a single `.bun-version` (bumped 1.3.12 → 1.3.14, the version local dev already ran — verified the worldgen digests hold across the bump, which the repo claimed but had never tested).

## Corrections to the original review

- **Invite consumption was reported as a non-atomic read-then-write race — it wasn't.** It's already a single conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE uses < max_uses RETURNING`. Two *different* nearby bugs were fixed instead (transaction + same-user double-consume).
- **Server-persistence loss was overstated** as "loses long stretches routinely." `join`/`leave`/`shutdown` all capture unmarked state on graceful paths; the real window is a hard crash mid-session.
- **The "critical" save-GET finding was reframed:** membership-gated reads are the documented design. The narrow, real defect was the missing `kind` check on `PUT`.
- **The 478ms whole-region remesh (chunked-meshing rewrite) is deferred, not done** — the number is unverified in a real frame, and it's a multi-session project. Left out deliberately.

## Deploy note

`0004` is additive and safe to run first; rolling the code back needs no down-migration. But **web and game server both write `save_revision`, so they must ship from the same SHA** — half-deployed, the un-updated side writes blobs without advancing the revision and no device sees the cloud move. Same shape as this repo's protocol-bump deploys (see `docs/deploy.md`).

## Verification

`lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `build`, `bun test` (1541 pass), and `test:e2e` (35 pass, incl. the multiplayer and nether-online journeys) all green on the branch tip. 13 commits, one logical slice each.

Done. **PR #65 is open:** https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/pull/65

## What shipped

13 commits on `fix/review-hardening`, one logical slice each, full gate green — **1541 unit tests, 35 e2e (including the multiplayer and nether-online journeys), plus build/lint/typecheck/format**.

The fixes, roughly by how likely they were to bite a real player:

- **Renaming a cloud world** silently disabled sync on your other devices — the cursor and the metadata mtime were the same column. Split into a `saveRevision` column (migration `0004`).
- **Backgrounding on a phone** conflicted with itself (`pagehide`+`visibilitychange` both fire). Fixed with a latest-wins push queue.
- **A network blip** could kill a session that had *already* reconnected. Fixed with a connection-generation guard.
- **A server crash** lost progress that involved no block edit (inventory, health, XP…). Occupied rooms now persist unconditionally on the interval.
- Plus the server-authority hole on save PUT, malformed-save crashes, the room-eviction race, frame reordering, world-creation validation, and the invite/resync hardening.

## Things worth knowing before you look

- **Two of Codex's findings were wrong or overstated**, and I said so in the PR body rather than implementing them: invite consumption was already atomic, and the server-persistence loss was narrower than "loses long stretches routinely."
- **The chunked-meshing rewrite is deferred, not done.** That 478ms remesh number is unverified in a real frame, and it's a multi-session project — not worth bundling into a correctness batch.
- **Deploy constraint:** migration `0004` is additive and safe to run first, but web and the Fly game server both write `save_revision`, so they must ship from the **same SHA** — same as your protocol-bump deploys. This is in the PR body and `docs/deploy.md`.

## Two process notes

- I found and fixed a bug **I introduced**: commit 8's first form made all inbound frames async and broke 16 emit-then-assert tests, because I ran a filtered test instead of the full NetworkSession suite before committing. Caught it at the next full run, amended commit 8 to keep it bisectable.
- Your standing memory says review-driven fixes stay local until you check them — I pushed and opened the PR because you told me to this session. Flagging so the override is explicit.

The two lint warnings throughout are pre-existing (`GameShell` set-state-in-effect), untouched by this branch.

codex has reviewed again find some new issues, what do you think? the review report is: ## Re-review outcome

  The branch is substantially improved, but I would not merge it yet. Three high-severity issues remain, including two
  upgrade paths that can lose saves.

  ### Findings

  1. High — The v1 → v2 cursor change can overwrite newer offline progress

     lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:23 deliberately starts with a fresh localStorage key. Any existing device therefore has no
     v2 cursor, so lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:134 treats it as a first download. components/GameShell.tsx:206 then
     overwrites the durable IndexedDB save.

     Reproduced: with a valid v1 cursor and no v2 cursor, the current code returns adopt: true.

     Scenario: play offline after the last successful upload, upgrade the app, then open the world. The older cloud save
     replaces the newer local progress.

     Preserve the v1 cursor for a transition release and distinguish “fresh download” from “existing local save with an
     unknown revision.” Ambiguous upgrades should retain local data or surface a conflict, never automatically overwrite
     it.

  2. High — Migration 0004 is not safe while the old web build is live

     The migration says an old build can ignore the new column in db/migrations/0004_save-revision.sql:15. That is
     structurally true but semantically unsafe: after migration, the old web build can update save_blob without
     incrementing save_revision.

     Consequences:
      - An existing device can miss the update because its revision appears unchanged.
      - An old first upload can leave save_blob != null with revision 0, allowing a new client’s “first upload” to
        overwrite it.

      - The independent Vercel and Fly jobs do not provide an atomic rollout; the Vercel hook returns before the new
        build is live in .github/workflows/ci.yml:75.

     Make the database own revision increments, such as with a trigger on save_blob, or enforce a real write-maintenance
     window. Add a migration test that applies 0004, performs an old-style blob update, and verifies the revision
     advances.

  3. High — Multiplayer authoritative blobs remain downloadable by members

     PUT is correctly restricted to sp-cloud, but lib/online/worldsService.ts:267 still returns blobs for both kinds,
     and the app/api/worlds/[id]/save/route.ts:15 exposes them.

     “The member can already play the world” is not equivalent access. The blob contains offline player slices,
     inventories, coordinates, both dimensions and world state that the member may never have observed.

     Restrict browser GET and PUT to sp-cloud. The authoritative server should access multiplayer persistence only
     through its database Adapter.

  4. Medium — Cloud decompression and upload validation are still insufficiently bounded

     Browser decompression materializes the complete output in lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:56. Uploads are stored without
     verifying gzip or save contents, and a lying/missing content length is rejected only after request.arrayBuffer()
     has allocated the complete body in the app/api/worlds/[id]/save/route.ts:49.

     The server-side bounded decoder is a good improvement, but its 96 MiB ceiling can still produce several hundred MiB
     of peak memory after chunks, merged bytes, string, parsed JSON and sanitized arrays coexist.

     Use a shared bounded save-envelope Module for browser and server decoding. Validate before storage and set limits
     from measured real save sizes.

  5. Medium — Other online request bodies still throw on hostile types

     World creation is now validated correctly, but profile creation, profile updates and world renaming still trust
     bare-cast JSON. I directly reproduced TypeError from all three with numeric names:
      - lib/online/worldsService.ts:89
      - lib/online/worldsService.ts:111
      - lib/online/worldsService.ts:245

     Add one untrusted-input decoding Module used by every online route, including profileId and skinId validation.

  6. Medium — Process shutdown still misses loading and evicting rooms

     server/roomRegistry.ts:102 waits only for rooms currently in rooms. A load can finish after shutdown starts, while
     an eviction’s final persistence can still be running when server/index.ts:131 calls process.exit(0).

     It should enter a terminal state, reject new loads, await loading and evicting, then shut down every resulting
     room. Persistence failures should also be logged and produce a bounded nonzero shutdown path rather than leaving
     the signal promise unresolved.

  7. Remaining earlier findings
      - The reset resurrection race remains: lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts:740 arms the unmount guard only after deletion
        completes.

      - Same-world multi-tab saves still use silent last-writer-wins behavior.
      - Account-level sp-cloud rows and invite creation remain uncapped, enabling storage growth.
      - Resync is now bounded per client, but three full syncs per second per connected client can still produce
        substantial synchronous gzip and socket-buffer pressure.

      - The P1 performance work is untouched: whole-region remeshing and synchronous client/server world creation remain
        the largest runtime costs.

  ### Confirmed good fixes

  The malformed-save crash, cloud push serialization, durable cursor commit, network frame ordering, reconnect
  idempotence, occupied-room persistence, overlapping-store coalescing, room eviction handoff, invite transaction,
  world-creation validation, documentation drift and Bun pinning are all materially improved and have appropriate
  regression tests.

  The new cloudPushQueue and persistence coordination have useful Depth and Locality. The next architectural step should
  be a shared save-envelope Module with browser/server Adapters and a RoomRegistry lifecycle Module that owns live/
  loading/evicting/terminal states behind one Interface.

  ### Verification

  - Typecheck, formatting and production build: passed.
  - Unit/integration/component: 1,541 passed, 0 failed.
  - Lint: passed with the same two GameShell warnings.
  - E2E did not start because another workspace process, agrippa/apps/api, owns port 3000. I left that process
    untouched.

  - Worktree remains clean; no files were changed.

# Review hardening: correctness, persistence, and concurrency

## Context

Codex reviewed the repo and filed a broad findings report. I verified every claim against the
source. Most hold up; two do not, and one buried finding is the most user-visible bug in the set.
This plan implements the confirmed findings, skips the false one, and defers the renderer rewrite.

**Corrections to the report, for the record:**

- **Invite consumption is already atomic** (`lib/online/worldsService.ts:328`) — a single conditional
  `UPDATE … WHERE uses < max_uses RETURNING` with a SQL-side increment. Not read-then-write. The
  finding as written is dropped; two smaller real bugs nearby are kept (below).
- **Server persistence loss is narrower than claimed.** `join` (`server/room.ts:461`), `leave` (`:527`)
  and `shutdown` (`:658`, which *awaits* `persist()`) all capture unmarked state on graceful paths.
  The real window is a hard crash mid-session. Still worth fixing; not "loses long stretches" routinely.
- **Save `GET` being membership-gated is intended**, per the module contract at `worldsService.ts:19-21`.
  The defect is narrower: `putSaveBlob` never checks `world.kind`.
- **The 478 ms remesh number is unverified in a real frame.** The full-region rebuild is real; the cost
  is not yet trustworthy. Gated behind a measurement (see Deferred).

**The buried lede:** `renameWorld` (`worldsService.ts:224`) bumps `worlds.updatedAt`, which is *also*
the save-revision cursor. Renaming a cloud world invalidates every device's cursor with no blob change.
The next push 409s, and that 409 latches `cloudConflictRef` (`useMinecraftGame.ts:346`), silently
disabling cloud sync for the rest of the session. No concurrency needed. The duplicate
`pagehide`+`visibilitychange` push on mobile backgrounding does the same thing to a single device.

**Scope decided with the user:** correctness batch now, chunked meshing deferred.

---

## Branch and commits

**One branch: `fix/review-hardening`. 11 commits.** Broad, risky, spans many systems → one reviewable
unit per AGENTS.md, and it lands as **one synchronized Vercel+Fly deploy**, which is what the migration
wants anyway (see the deploy note below).

Granularity rule: **one commit per logical slice** (AGENTS.md), which in practice means merge wherever
one honest subject line covers the change, and stop where it would take an "and". Order puts cheap
independent work first so a late snag in the invasive commits doesn't strand it.

I now have full confirmation of every claim. Here is my verification report.

---

# Verification report — branch `fix/review-hardening`

The commit that renamed the key is `720616d` ("feat(db): add worlds.saveRevision as the save cursor"). Its own message states: *"Client stamps move to minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2 rather than migrating ... Starting empty costs nothing, because the open-time pull sets a cursor before anything pushes."* That last assumption is the crux of the data-loss claim, and it is wrong for a specific case (see claims 4/5).

## Claim 1 — `readStamps` / `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` / `pushSave` / `fetchCloudSave` — TRUE

The single storage key is v2 only, and `readStamps` reads exclusively it:

- `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:29` — `const STAMPS_KEY = "minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2";`
- `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:33-35` — `readStamps` does `JSON.parse(storage.getItem(STAMPS_KEY) ?? "{}")`. There is no read of `_v1` anywhere in the repo. A grep across the tree finds only `_v2` (in `cloudSaves.ts`, its test, and the e2e). No migration/backfill from `_v1` exists — the fresh-key choice is confirmed.
- `pushSave` — `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:74-97`. Reads `const base = readStamps(storage)[cloudWorldId]` (line 79) and sends `"x-base-revision": base === undefined ? "" : String(base)` (line 85).
- `fetchCloudSave` — `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:100-111`. Parses `x-save-revision` header (line 104), returns `{ save, saveRevision }` or `null`.
- `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` — `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:134-142`.

## Claim 2 — trace: valid v1 entry, NO v2 entry, server `x-save-revision: 5` → `adopt: true` — TRUE

Step by step through `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` (`lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:134-142`):

1. Line 135 — `fetchCloudSave` returns `{ save, saveRevision: 5 }` (header `"5"` parses to integer 5, so `Number.isInteger(header)` → `saveRevision: 5`, line 107).
2. Line 136 — `result` is truthy, not `{ adopt: false }`.
3. Line 137 — `const cursor = readStamps(storage)[cloudWorldId]`. `readStamps` reads only `minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2` (line 35). The device has **no v2 entry**, so `cursor === undefined`. **The v1 entry is never consulted.**
4. Line 138 — `revision = 5`.
5. Line 139 — `revision === null`? No.
6. Line 140 — `cursor !== undefined && revision <= cursor` → `cursor` **is** `undefined`, so the whole condition is `false`; does not return.
7. Line 141 — returns `{ adopt: true, save: result.save, commitCursor: () => writeStamp(cloudWorldId, 5, storage) }`.

Result: **`{ adopt: true }`**. The pre-existing v1 stamp is dead weight; the device behaves exactly like a first-ever download.

## Claim 3 — `openWorld` / `playCloud` overwrite the local IndexedDB save on adopt — TRUE

`components/GameShell.tsx`:

- `openWorld` — lines 207-213:
  ```
  if (decision.adopt) {
    await worldSaves.write(worldId, decision.save);
    decision.commitCursor();
  }
  ```
  `worldSaves.write(worldId, decision.save)` (line 211) writes the **cloud** blob into local IndexedDB under the world's key. This is an unconditional overwrite — the local save is replaced by `decision.save`; the prior local contents are not read, merged, or preserved.
- `playCloud` — lines 246-249: same pattern, `await worldSaves.write(`cloud:${world.id}`, decision.save)` (line 247).

So yes: on `adopt: true`, the local IndexedDB save **is overwritten** by the cloud save.

## Claim 4 — offline local progress made after last upload is overwritten by the older cloud save on first open after upgrade — TRUE (data-loss claim CONFIRMED)

Chaining claims 2 + 3 for the exact scenario (device synced before the upgrade, then made offline local progress that was never pushed, so the cloud blob is still at its last-uploaded revision, e.g. 5; app upgrades, so the `_v2` key is empty):

- First open → `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` → `cursor === undefined` (v2 empty) → **skips the guard at `cloudSaves.ts:140`** → returns `{ adopt: true }` with the revision-5 cloud save.

const save = this.composeSave();

""`, so a numeric `name` reaches `.trim()`.

All three route bodies are bare casts with no runtime type check before the service call.

**FALSE — not validated for type or length anywhere.**

`skinId`:
- `createProfile:104` — stored as `skinId: input.skinId ?? null`, no type or length check.

# Review hardening — round 2 (re-review of PR #65)

## Context

Codex re-reviewed the open PR #65 (`fix/review-hardening`). I verified every claim against the
branch. The batch is "substantially improved" but has issues that should land before merge —
including **one data-loss regression I introduced** in round 1. These fixes go on the **same
branch** as follow-up commits (they update PR #65; no new PR).

**Verified findings, by severity:**

- **#1 (HIGH — data-loss regression, MINE).** Round 1's commit `720616d` moved the client sync
  cursor to a *fresh* localStorage key (`minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2`). An upgraded device has no v2
  cursor, so `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` (`lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:134`) treats it as a first download and
  `GameShell` overwrites the durable IndexedDB save with the *older* cloud copy. Scenario: play
  offline after your last upload, upgrade, reopen → newer local progress destroyed. My commit
  comment ("starting empty costs nothing, the pull sets a cursor before anything pushes") was wrong:
  the pull **adopts (overwrites) before** it sets the cursor. Verified `adopt: true` for a device
  with a v1 cursor and no v2 cursor. Constraint on the fix (also verified): you can't just "keep
  local and let the next push reconcile" — with no v2 cursor, `pushSave` sends `x-base-revision: ""`,
  which the server treats as a first upload (requires revision 0) and **409s forever** against an
  already-saved world. The fix must seed a v2 cursor without overwriting local.

- **#2 (HIGH — deploy-window unsafety).** `save_revision` is incremented by app code only
  (`putSaveBlob` + `storeWorld`, both `sql\`… + 1\``); there is no DB trigger. So after migration
  0004 runs, an **old** web build still serving would write `save_blob` without bumping
  `save_revision` — a device could miss the update, and an old first-upload could leave
  `save_blob != null` at revision 0 (which a new client's "first upload" then overwrites). The two
  deploy jobs aren't atomic. Verified: PGlite supports plpgsql, and no trigger exists yet.

- **#3 (HIGH — info disclosure).** `putSaveBlob` is `sp-cloud`-gated but `getSaveBlob`
  (`worldsService.ts:267`) returns the blob for **both** kinds. An `mp` blob is the whole
  authoritative world: every (incl. offline) player's inventory/coords/health/XP/stats and *both*
  dimensions. Any invited member can GET state they never observed in-game. Verified nothing
  legitimate GETs an mp blob from the browser (the client only pulls `sp-cloud`; the game server
  reads via direct Postgres, never the HTTP route) — so restricting GET to `sp-cloud` is free. This
  reverses my round-1 "GET stays membership-gated by design" call; codex is right that blob access ≠
  in-game visibility.

- **#5 (MEDIUM — 500s on hostile input).** `createProfile` (`:94`), `updateProfile` (`:118`), and
  `renameWorld` (`:246`) call `.trim()` on bare-cast JSON and throw `TypeError` (→ 500) on a numeric
  name. Their routes bare-cast the body. `skinId`/`profileId` are never type/length validated. Same
  class as the round-1 `createWorld` fix, which already has the guard pattern to copy.

- **#6 (MEDIUM — shutdown misses rooms).** `shutdownAll` (`roomRegistry.ts:102`) awaits only rooms
  in `rooms`, not `loading` or `evicting`. A load finishing after shutdown starts, or an eviction's
  final persist still running, is missed before `process.exit(0)` (`server/index.ts:131`).

- **#7a (MEDIUM — reset resurrection, carried from round 1).** `resetNow`
  (`useMinecraftGame.ts:740`) arms `skipUnmountSaveRef` **after** the async delete, so an autosave/
  flush in the deletion window can rewrite the just-deleted blob. `dimensionTravel` (`:492`) already
  arms **before** its write with a comment saying why; `resetNow` should mirror it.

**Deferred (with rationale), not in this round:**

- **#4 (decompression bounds).** Browser `gunzipJson` materializes full output (player's own machine,
  own save — low risk), and the server's 96 MiB ceiling is generous. The live server vector is
  already closed (mp blobs are server-written only). Lowering the ceiling without measured real-save
  sizes risks rejecting a legitimate huge build. Left as a tuning item; a shared save-envelope module
  is more than three call sites warrant now.
- **#7b–d.** Account-level `sp-cloud` / invite-creation caps (storage-growth product decision, not
  correctness); resync already bounded (3/s/client — further tuning is minor); multi-tab
  last-writer-wins; and the P1 perf work (whole-region remesh) — the big deferred item, unchanged.

---

## The fixes (6 commits, same branch)

Order: the two data-safety blockers first, then the cheap correctness items.

### 1. `fix(game): don't overwrite newer local progress on cursor upgrade` (finding #1)

The cursor being absent must not mean "first download" when a durable local save exists. Discriminate
on **local-save existence**, not just the cursor.

- `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` — `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` takes a `hasLocalSave` hint. When there is **no
  v2 cursor**:
  - `hasLocalSave` true → **keep local** (`adopt: false`) and **seed the v2 cursor** from the current
    remote revision. This reduces the device to the normal "has a cursor" flow: the next `pushSave`
    uses `base = R` (bumps to R+1, uploads the newer local), and any genuine cross-device conflict
    routes through the existing push-side 409 + warning — never a silent overwrite.
  - `hasLocalSave` false → `adopt: true` (genuine fresh device / re-download — unchanged).
- `components/GameShell.tsx` — `openWorld` (`:206`) and `playCloud` (`:239`) pass whether a durable
  local save exists (reuse `worldSaves.read`, already imported; a null result = no local save). The
  seeding is a plain `writeStamp`, so no `commitCursor` is owed on the keep-local branch.
- Keep the `minecraft_cloud_stamps_v1` key readable is **not** required by this design — the
  local-save existence check is the correct discriminator and covers the re-download edge (v1 cursor
  present but local deleted) that a v1-cursor check would get wrong.

Tests (`cloudSaves.test.ts`): no-v2-cursor + hasLocalSave → `adopt: false` and the v2 cursor gets
seeded to the remote revision; no cursor + no local → adopt; the seeded device's next push is not a
first-upload 409. Add one that reproduces the loss against the current code.

### 2. `fix(db): let the database own save_revision via a trigger` (finding #2)

Move the increment off app code and onto the row, so *any* writer (new build, old build mid-deploy,
the game server) bumps it correctly — which also removes the same-SHA deploy constraint for this
column and closes the "old first-upload at revision 0" hole.

- New migration `db/migrations/0005_save-revision-trigger.sql`: a `BEFORE UPDATE ON worlds` trigger
  (plpgsql) that sets `save_revision = OLD.save_revision + 1` when `save_blob IS DISTINCT FROM
  OLD.save_blob`. Generate the drizzle journal entry alongside (hand-written SQL — drizzle won't
  emit a trigger).
- Drop the app-side `saveRevision: sql\`… + 1\`` from `putSaveBlob` (`worldsService.ts:324`) and
  `storeWorld` (`server/persistence.ts:110`). The CAS guard (`WHERE save_revision = base`) stays; the
  trigger does the increment; `RETURNING save_revision` returns the new value. `renameWorld` (no
  `save_blob` change) still doesn't bump — now structurally, not by omission.
- Mirror the trigger into `db/ddl.ts` (the hand-written test/dev schema).
- `db/migrations.test.ts`: apply through 0005, do an **old-style** blob update
  (`SET save_blob = …` only, no `save_revision`), assert the revision advanced; assert a rename does
  not bump.

### 3. `fix(online): restrict save-blob GET to sp-cloud worlds` (finding #3)

- `getSaveBlob` (`worldsService.ts:267`): select the world row (already does) and
  `if (world.kind !== "sp-cloud") return fail("invalid")`, mirroring `putSaveBlob`. Update the module
  docstring, which currently implies only writes are kind-gated.
- Test: a member GET on an `mp` world → `invalid`; `sp-cloud` GET still works.

### 4. `fix(online): validate profile and rename request bodies` (finding #5)

- `createProfile` / `updateProfile` / `renameWorld`: `typeof … !== "string"` guards before `.trim()`
  (copy the `createWorld:180` pattern), reuse the existing `MAX_PROFILE_NAME` / name-length caps, and
  type-check `skinId` (string-or-null). Targeted guards, not a new validation module (three sites).
- Tests: numeric name → `invalid` (not a throw) for each; non-string `skinId` rejected.

### 5. `fix(server): drain loading and evicting rooms on shutdown` (finding #6)

- `roomRegistry.ts`: a `shuttingDown` flag; `getOrLoad` returns `null` once set (no new loads).
  `shutdownAll` awaits the in-flight `loading` promises (so they land in `rooms`) and the `evicting`
  promises, then shuts down every resulting room. Use `allSettled` and log failures so one bad
  persist can't strand the exit.
- Test (`roomRegistry.test.ts`): a load in flight when `shutdownAll` starts is still shut down; an
  in-flight eviction is awaited.

### 6. `fix(game): arm the reset skip-guard before deletion` (finding #7a)

- `useMinecraftGame.ts` `resetNow`: set `skipUnmountSaveRef.current = true` **before**
  `worldSaves.remove(...)`, and disarm on failure — mirroring `dimensionTravel` (`:492`).

---

## Verification

Per fix: `bun run format` + `bun run lint` locally.

Before pushing to PR #65, the full gate: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`,
`bun test`, `bun run build`, and `bun run test:e2e`. **Check `lsof -ti:3000` first** — codex's e2e run
was blocked by another project's dev server on port 3000 (a known repo gotcha; use the alt-port
trick if busy).

End-to-end checks beyond the suites:

1. **#1:** simulate an upgraded device — a world with a durable local save, a v1 cursor, and no v2
   cursor, where local is newer than the cloud. Open it: local must survive, and a subsequent push
   must not 409. (The `cloudSaves.e2e.ts` round-trip already exercises the happy path; extend or add a
   unit-level reproduction.)
2. **#2:** the migration test above — an old-style blob update bumps the revision.
3. **#3:** two accounts on an `mp` world; the member's `GET /api/worlds/:id/save` is refused.
4. **#6:** covered by the registry unit test (real timers not needed).

Deploy note is unchanged in shape but **relaxed by fix #2**: with the trigger owning the increment,
web and Fly no longer must ship from the same SHA for `save_revision` correctness — the migration
(0005) just needs to run, and any build writes correct revisions. Migration 0005 is additive
(trigger only); rollback needs no down-migration.

# Review hardening — round 2 (re-review of PR #65)

## Context

Codex re-reviewed the open PR #65 (`fix/review-hardening`). I verified every claim against the
branch. The batch is "substantially improved" but has issues that should land before merge —
including **one data-loss regression I introduced** in round 1. These fixes go on the **same
branch** as follow-up commits (they update PR #65; no new PR).

**Verified findings, by severity:**

- **#1 (HIGH — data-loss regression, MINE).** Round 1's commit `720616d` moved the client sync
  cursor to a *fresh* localStorage key (`minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2`). An upgraded device has no v2
  cursor, so `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` (`lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:134`) treats it as a first download and
  `GameShell` overwrites the durable IndexedDB save with the *older* cloud copy. Scenario: play
  offline after your last upload, upgrade, reopen → newer local progress destroyed. My commit
  comment ("starting empty costs nothing, the pull sets a cursor before anything pushes") was wrong:
  the pull **adopts (overwrites) before** it sets the cursor. Verified `adopt: true` for a device
  with a v1 cursor and no v2 cursor. Constraint on the fix (also verified): you can't just "keep
  local and let the next push reconcile" — with no v2 cursor, `pushSave` sends `x-base-revision: ""`,
  which the server treats as a first upload (requires revision 0) and **409s forever** against an
  already-saved world. The fix must seed a v2 cursor without overwriting local.

- **#2 (HIGH — deploy-window unsafety).** `save_revision` is incremented by app code only
  (`putSaveBlob` + `storeWorld`, both `sql\`… + 1\``); there is no DB trigger. So after migration
  0004 runs, an **old** web build still serving would write `save_blob` without bumping
  `save_revision` — a device could miss the update, and an old first-upload could leave
  `save_blob != null` at revision 0 (which a new client's "first upload" then overwrites). The two
  deploy jobs aren't atomic. Verified: PGlite supports plpgsql, and no trigger exists yet.

- **#3 (HIGH — info disclosure).** `putSaveBlob` is `sp-cloud`-gated but `getSaveBlob`
  (`worldsService.ts:267`) returns the blob for **both** kinds. An `mp` blob is the whole
  authoritative world: every (incl. offline) player's inventory/coords/health/XP/stats and *both*
  dimensions. Any invited member can GET state they never observed in-game. Verified nothing
  legitimate GETs an mp blob from the browser (the client only pulls `sp-cloud`; the game server
  reads via direct Postgres, never the HTTP route) — so restricting GET to `sp-cloud` is free. This
  reverses my round-1 "GET stays membership-gated by design" call; codex is right that blob access ≠
  in-game visibility.

- **#5 (MEDIUM — 500s on hostile input).** `createProfile` (`:94`), `updateProfile` (`:118`), and
  `renameWorld` (`:246`) call `.trim()` on bare-cast JSON and throw `TypeError` (→ 500) on a numeric
  name. Their routes bare-cast the body. `skinId`/`profileId` are never type/length validated. Same
  class as the round-1 `createWorld` fix, which already has the guard pattern to copy.

- **#6 (MEDIUM — shutdown misses rooms).** `shutdownAll` (`roomRegistry.ts:102`) awaits only rooms
  in `rooms`, not `loading` or `evicting`. A load finishing after shutdown starts, or an eviction's
  final persist still running, is missed before `process.exit(0)` (`server/index.ts:131`).

- **#7a (MEDIUM — reset resurrection, carried from round 1).** `resetNow`
  (`useMinecraftGame.ts:740`) arms `skipUnmountSaveRef` **after** the async delete, so an autosave/
  flush in the deletion window can rewrite the just-deleted blob. `dimensionTravel` (`:492`) already
  arms **before** its write with a comment saying why; `resetNow` should mirror it.

**Deferred (with rationale), not in this round:**

- **#4 (decompression bounds).** Browser `gunzipJson` materializes full output (player's own machine,
  own save — low risk), and the server's 96 MiB ceiling is generous. The live server vector is
  already closed (mp blobs are server-written only). Lowering the ceiling without measured real-save
  sizes risks rejecting a legitimate huge build. Left as a tuning item; a shared save-envelope module
  is more than three call sites warrant now.
- **#7b–d.** Account-level `sp-cloud` / invite-creation caps (storage-growth product decision, not
  correctness); resync already bounded (3/s/client — further tuning is minor); multi-tab
  last-writer-wins; and the P1 perf work (whole-region remesh) — the big deferred item, unchanged.

---

## The fixes (6 commits, same branch)

Order: the two data-safety blockers first, then the cheap correctness items.

### 1. `fix(game): don't overwrite newer local progress on cursor upgrade` (finding #1)

The cursor being absent must not mean "first download" when a durable local save exists. Discriminate
on **local-save existence**, not just the cursor.

- `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` — `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` takes a `hasLocalSave` hint. When there is **no
  v2 cursor**:
  - `hasLocalSave` true → **keep local** (`adopt: false`) and **seed the v2 cursor** from the current
    remote revision. This reduces the device to the normal "has a cursor" flow: the next `pushSave`
    uses `base = R` (bumps to R+1, uploads the newer local), and any genuine cross-device conflict
    routes through the existing push-side 409 + warning — never a silent overwrite.
  - `hasLocalSave` false → `adopt: true` (genuine fresh device / re-download — unchanged).
- `components/GameShell.tsx` — `openWorld` (`:206`) and `playCloud` (`:239`) pass whether a durable
  local save exists (reuse `worldSaves.read`, already imported; a null result = no local save). The
  seeding is a plain `writeStamp`, so no `commitCursor` is owed on the keep-local branch.
- Keep the `minecraft_cloud_stamps_v1` key readable is **not** required by this design — the
  local-save existence check is the correct discriminator and covers the re-download edge (v1 cursor
  present but local deleted) that a v1-cursor check would get wrong.

Tests (`cloudSaves.test.ts`): no-v2-cursor + hasLocalSave → `adopt: false` and the v2 cursor gets
seeded to the remote revision; no cursor + no local → adopt; the seeded device's next push is not a
first-upload 409. Add one that reproduces the loss against the current code.

### 2. `fix(db): let the database own save_revision via a trigger` (finding #2)

- `createProfile` (`:94`) / `updateProfile` (`:119`) / `renameWorld` (`:246`): `typeof … !== "string"`

- The routes (`app/api/profiles/route.ts`, `app/api/profiles/[id]/route.ts`, `app/api/worlds/[id]/route.ts`)

- Tests: numeric name → `invalid` (not a throw) for each; unknown/non-string `skinId` rejected.

### 5. `fix(server): drain loading and evicting rooms on shutdown` (finding #6)

- `roomRegistry.ts`: a `shuttingDown` flag; `getOrLoad` returns `null` once set (no new loads).

# Review hardening — round 2 (re-review of PR #65)

## Context

Codex re-reviewed the open PR #65 (`fix/review-hardening`). I verified every claim against the
branch. The batch is "substantially improved" but has issues that should land before merge —
including **one data-loss regression I introduced** in round 1. These fixes go on the **same
branch** as follow-up commits (they update PR #65; no new PR).

**Verified findings, by severity:**

- **#1 (HIGH — data-loss regression, MINE).** Round 1's commit `720616d` moved the client sync
  cursor to a *fresh* localStorage key (`minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2`). An upgraded device has no v2
  cursor, so `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` (`lib/game/cloudSaves.ts:134`) treats it as a first download and
  `GameShell` overwrites the durable IndexedDB save with the *older* cloud copy. Scenario: play
  offline after your last upload, upgrade, reopen → newer local progress destroyed. My commit
  comment ("starting empty costs nothing, the pull sets a cursor before anything pushes") was wrong:
  the pull **adopts (overwrites) before** it sets the cursor. Verified `adopt: true` for a device
  with a v1 cursor and no v2 cursor. Constraint on the fix (also verified): you can't just "keep
  local and let the next push reconcile" — with no v2 cursor, `pushSave` sends `x-base-revision: ""`,
  which the server treats as a first upload (requires revision 0) and **409s forever** against an
  already-saved world. The fix must seed a v2 cursor without overwriting local.

- **#2 (HIGH — deploy-window unsafety).** `save_revision` is incremented by app code only
  (`putSaveBlob` + `storeWorld`, both `sql\`… + 1\``); there is no DB trigger. So after migration
  0004 runs, an **old** web build still serving would write `save_blob` without bumping
  `save_revision` — a device could miss the update, and an old first-upload could leave
  `save_blob != null` at revision 0 (which a new client's "first upload" then overwrites). The two
  deploy jobs aren't atomic. Verified: PGlite supports plpgsql, and no trigger exists yet.

- **#3 (HIGH — info disclosure).** `putSaveBlob` is `sp-cloud`-gated but `getSaveBlob`
  (`worldsService.ts:267`) returns the blob for **both** kinds. An `mp` blob is the whole
  authoritative world: every (incl. offline) player's inventory/coords/health/XP/stats and *both*
  dimensions. Any invited member can GET state they never observed in-game. Verified nothing
  legitimate GETs an mp blob from the browser (the client only pulls `sp-cloud`; the game server
  reads via direct Postgres, never the HTTP route) — so restricting GET to `sp-cloud` is free. This
  reverses my round-1 "GET stays membership-gated by design" call; codex is right that blob access ≠
  in-game visibility.

- **#5 (MEDIUM — 500s on hostile input).** `createProfile` (`:94`), `updateProfile` (`:118`), and
  `renameWorld` (`:246`) call `.trim()` on bare-cast JSON and throw `TypeError` (→ 500) on a numeric
  name. Their routes bare-cast the body. `skinId`/`profileId` are never type/length validated. Same
  class as the round-1 `createWorld` fix, which already has the guard pattern to copy.

- **#6 (MEDIUM — shutdown misses rooms).** `shutdownAll` (`roomRegistry.ts:102`) awaits only rooms
  in `rooms`, not `loading` or `evicting`. A load finishing after shutdown starts, or an eviction's
  final persist still running, is missed before `process.exit(0)` (`server/index.ts:131`).

- **#7a (MEDIUM — reset resurrection, carried from round 1).** `resetNow`
  (`useMinecraftGame.ts:740`) arms `skipUnmountSaveRef` **after** the async delete, so an autosave/
  flush in the deletion window can rewrite the just-deleted blob. `dimensionTravel` (`:492`) already
  arms **before** its write with a comment saying why; `resetNow` should mirror it.

**Deferred (with rationale), not in this round:**

- **#4 (decompression bounds).** Browser `gunzipJson` materializes full output (player's own machine,
  own save — low risk), and the server's 96 MiB ceiling is generous. The live server vector is
  already closed (mp blobs are server-written only). Lowering the ceiling without measured real-save
  sizes risks rejecting a legitimate huge build. Left as a tuning item; a shared save-envelope module
  is more than three call sites warrant now.
- **#7b–d.** Account-level `sp-cloud` / invite-creation caps (storage-growth product decision, not
  correctness); resync already bounded (3/s/client — further tuning is minor); multi-tab
  last-writer-wins; and the P1 perf work (whole-region remesh) — the big deferred item, unchanged.

## The fixes (2 commits, same branch)

PR #65 squash-merges, so all branch commits collapse to one on `main` regardless — branch granularity

_(Detailed under "2." below.)_

### COMMIT B — the five app-level fixes

### 1. `fix(game): don't overwrite newer local progress on cursor upgrade` (finding #1)

The cursor being absent must not mean "first download" when a durable local save exists. Discriminate

  v2 cursor**:
  - `hasLocalSave` true → **keep local** (`adopt: false`) and **seed the v2 cursor** from the current

    uses `base = R` (bumps to R+1, uploads the newer local), and any genuine cross-device conflict
    routes through the existing push-side 409 + warning — never a silent overwrite.

  local save exists (reuse `worldSaves.read`, already imported; a null result = no local save). The
  seeding is a plain `writeStamp`, so no `commitCursor` is owed on the keep-local branch.
- Keep the `minecraft_cloud_stamps_v1` key readable is **not** required by this design — the
  local-save existence check is the correct discriminator and covers the re-download edge (v1 cursor
  present but local deleted) that a v1-cursor check would get wrong.

seeded to the remote revision; no cursor + no local → adopt; the seeded device's next push is not a

column and closes the "old first-upload at revision 0" hole.

  (plpgsql) that sets `save_revision = OLD.save_revision + 1` when `save_blob IS DISTINCT FROM
  OLD.save_blob`. Generate the drizzle journal entry alongside (hand-written SQL — drizzle won't
  emit a trigger).

  `storeWorld` (`server/persistence.ts:110`). The CAS guard (`WHERE save_revision = base`) stays; the
  trigger does the increment; `RETURNING save_revision` returns the new value. `renameWorld` (no
  `save_blob` change) still doesn't bump — now structurally, not by omission.
- Mirror the trigger into `db/ddl.ts` (the hand-written test/dev schema).
- `db/migrations.test.ts`: apply through 0005, do an **old-style** blob update
  (`SET save_blob = …` only, no `save_revision`), assert the revision advanced; assert a rename does
  not bump.

### 3. `fix(online): restrict save-blob GET to sp-cloud worlds` (finding #3)

- `getSaveBlob` (`worldsService.ts:267`): select the world row (already does) and
  `if (world.kind !== "sp-cloud") return fail("invalid")`, mirroring `putSaveBlob`. Update the module
  docstring, which currently implies only writes are kind-gated.
- Test: a member GET on an `mp` world → `invalid`; `sp-cloud` GET still works.

### 4. `fix(online): validate profile and rename request bodies` (finding #5)

- `createProfile` (`:94`) / `updateProfile` (`:119`) / `renameWorld` (`:246`): `typeof … !== "string"`
  guards before `.trim()` (copy the `createWorld:180` pattern), reuse the existing `MAX_PROFILE_NAME`
  / name caps. For `skinId`, reject non-`string`/non-`null`, and reuse the existing `isSkinId` guard
  (already used at `GameShell.tsx:52`) so an unknown skin can't be stored. Targeted guards, not a new
  validation module (three sites).
- The routes (`app/api/profiles/route.ts`, `app/api/profiles/[id]/route.ts`, `app/api/worlds/[id]/route.ts`)
  bare-cast the body — leave them thin; the service is the validation boundary, as with `createWorld`.
- Tests: numeric name → `invalid` (not a throw) for each; unknown/non-string `skinId` rejected.

### 5. `fix(server): drain loading and evicting rooms on shutdown` (finding #6)

- `roomRegistry.ts`: a `shuttingDown` flag; `getOrLoad` returns `null` once set (no new loads).
  `shutdownAll` awaits the in-flight `loading` promises (so they land in `rooms`) and the `evicting`
  promises, then shuts down every resulting room. Use `allSettled` and log failures so one bad
  persist can't strand the exit.
- Test (`roomRegistry.test.ts`): a load in flight when `shutdownAll` starts is still shut down; an
  in-flight eviction is awaited.

### 6. `fix(game): arm the reset skip-guard before deletion` (finding #7a)

- `useMinecraftGame.ts` `resetNow`: set `skipUnmountSaveRef.current = true` **before**
  `worldSaves.remove(...)`, and disarm on failure — mirroring `dimensionTravel` (`:492`).

Per fix: `bun run format` + `bun run lint` locally.

Before pushing to PR #65, the full gate: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`,
`bun test`, `bun run build`, and `bun run test:e2e`. **Check `lsof -ti:3000` first** — codex's e2e run
was blocked by another project's dev server on port 3000 (a known repo gotcha; use the alt-port

   unit-level reproduction.)
2. **#2:** the migration test above — an old-style blob update bumps the revision.
3. **#3:** two accounts on an `mp` world; the member's `GET /api/worlds/:id/save` is refused.
4. **#6:** covered by the registry unit test (real timers not needed).

-- Make the database own the save_revision increment.
--
-- 0004 split the cursor out of updated_at, but left the +1 to application code
-- (putSaveBlob and the game server's storeWorld). That is not deploy-safe: after
-- 0004 runs, an OLD web build still serving would update save_blob WITHOUT
-- bumping save_revision, so another device sees an unchanged revision and misses
-- the write — and an old first-upload could leave save_blob non-null at revision
-- 0, which a new client then treats as "never saved" and overwrites.
--
-- A BEFORE UPDATE trigger moves the increment onto the row, so EVERY writer — new
-- build, old build mid-deploy, the game server — bumps it correctly, and the web
-- and game-server deploys no longer have to be same-SHA for this column. It also
-- makes the "rename does not bump" rule structural rather than by-omission: a
-- rename changes name/updated_at but not save_blob, so IS DISTINCT FROM is false
-- and the revision holds. IS DISTINCT FROM (not =) so a first upload
-- (NULL -> blob) counts as a change and bumps 0 -> 1.
CREATE FUNCTION bump_save_revision() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.save_blob IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.save_blob THEN
    NEW.save_revision := OLD.save_revision + 1;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER worlds_bump_save_revision
  BEFORE UPDATE ON "worlds"
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION bump_save_revision();

+// 0005 moves the save_revision increment onto a DB trigger so ANY writer bumps
+// it — the whole point is that a build which doesn't set save_revision (an old
+// web build mid-deploy) still gets a correct increment. The test therefore does
+// OLD-STYLE updates (save_blob only, no save_revision) and checks the row.
+test("0005 trigger bumps save_revision on any blob change, and only on a blob change", async () => {
+  const pg = new PGlite();
+  for (const file of migrationFiles()) await applyMigration(pg, file);
+  await pg.exec(`INSERT INTO "user" (id, name, email) VALUES ('u1','u','u@e.com');`);
+  await pg.exec(`INSERT INTO worlds (id, owner_id, kind, name, seed, worldgen_version) VALUES ('w','u1','sp-cloud','W',1,12);`);
+  const revision = async () => (await pg.query<{ save_revision: number }>("SELECT save_revision FROM worlds WHERE id='w'")).rows[0].save_revision;
+  expect(await revision()).toBe(0); // never saved
+  // A first upload the OLD way: sets save_blob but not save_revision.
+  await pg.exec(`UPDATE worlds SET save_blob = '\\x01'::bytea, updated_at = now() WHERE id='w';`);
+  expect(await revision()).toBe(1); // NULL -> blob is a change (IS DISTINCT FROM), so 0 -> 1
+  await pg.exec(`UPDATE worlds SET save_blob = '\\x02'::bytea WHERE id='w';`);
+  expect(await revision()).toBe(2); // a different blob bumps
+  // A rename touches name/updated_at but not save_blob → must NOT bump the cursor.
+  await pg.exec(`UPDATE worlds SET name = 'Renamed', updated_at = now() WHERE id='w';`);
+  expect(await revision()).toBe(2);
+  // A byte-identical re-upload is a no-op — nothing changed, so no bump.
+  await pg.exec(`UPDATE worlds SET save_blob = '\\x02'::bytea, updated_at = now() WHERE id='w';`);
+  expect(await revision()).toBe(2);

**Two clocks, deliberately.** `worlds.updatedAt` is metadata mtime — "last
touched", what the world list orders by. `worlds.saveRevision` counts **blob
writes and nothing else**: it is the sync cursor devices compare (stored per
world under `minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2`) and the CAS token their uploads race
on, incremented SQL-side by both writers (`putSaveBlob` and the game server's
`storeWorld`) so concurrent writes can't settle on a value read earlier.
Revision `0` means never saved, which is what makes "first upload" checkable
without trusting the client. They must stay separate: while `updatedAt` served
as both, **renaming a world moved every other device's cursor** and 409'd its
next push over a save that hadn't changed — and since a 409 latches
`cloudConflictRef`, that silently disabled sync for the rest of the session.
Because revisions are ordered, the open-time reconcile asks whether the remote
is strictly _ahead_ of the cursor rather than merely different, so a remote
that's behind (a restored backup) leaves newer local progress alone.

⚠️ **The web app and the game server both write `save_revision`**, so they ship
from the same SHA — see [deploy.md](deploy.md#updating-a-running-deployment).

16	### Fixed
17	
18	- **Invite acceptance is now transactional, and resync requests are rate-limited**: two smaller online-server fixes. Accepting an invite consumed a use and then inserted the membership as two separate statements, so a failed insert burned a use with nothing to show for it, and two accepts from the _same_ user racing each other both passed a read-side "already a member?" check and each consumed a use — leaving two uses spent for the one membership the unique index actually created. The membership insert now goes first inside a transaction: concurrent same-user accepts dedupe on the index (the loser consumes nothing), and a use is spent if and only if a membership is granted. Separately, the `resync` message — which serializes and gzips a room's entire world diff — had no rate limit, so a hand-rolled client could loop it and stack full-world gzips against the 20 Hz tick loop every room in the process shares; it's now budgeted per second like the `cmd`/`chat`/`attack` messages. (No legitimate client sends `resync` in a loop; both are hardening against a crafted one.)
19	- **`POST /api/worlds` validates its body instead of trusting it**: the create-world handler cast the request JSON straight to its input type and passed it on, and the service checked only the name, kind, and that the seed was finite. So a hand-rolled request could set `worldType`/`gameMode`/`difficulty` to anything — the columns have no DB-level enum and the game server casts them straight into the engine at room boot — send a seed past int4 (a Postgres overflow surfaced as a 500, not a clean rejection), or set a non-string name that threw on `.trim()`. It now validates each field through the same `isWorldType`/`isGameMode`/`isDifficulty` guards the client already uses, bounds the seed to the column's range, and type-checks the rest. It also closes a **quota bypass**: `MAX_WORLDS_PER_PROFILE` was only checked when a `profileId` was supplied, so omitting it created uncapped, profile-less worlds — `mp` worlds (always profile-scoped in the UI) now require one, while `sp-cloud` stays account-level for the upload path. Nothing legitimate changes; the real client always sent valid values.
20	- **A brief network blip in an online world reconnects cleanly instead of sometimes killing the session**: the client's socket-close handling wasn't idempotent. A browser fires **both** `error` and `close` for an abnormal drop, and both ran the same close path — so one blip scheduled two reconnects, burned two rungs of the back-off ladder, minted two tickets, and raced two handshakes. The second handshake's join then kicked the first connection (`CLOSE_KICKED`, a fatal code), and because that orphaned socket's handlers were still bound, its close drove the session that had _just reconnected_ straight to "disconnected". A transient blip could therefore take down a session that had already recovered. Each socket now carries a connection generation: a close is acted on only for the live generation (a superseded socket's late close is ignored), and acting on one advances the generation so the same socket's error+close pair schedules exactly one reconnect. The reconnect timer is also single — a new rung clears any pending one rather than orphaning it. (Networking-only; no protocol or save change.)
21	- **Rejoining a world just as it's evicted can no longer resurrect it from stale state**: an idle room was dropped from the registry _before_ its shutdown finished persisting, and that final write is a whole-world gzip plus a Postgres round-trip — a window wide enough to land in. A join arriving inside it found no room, took the load path, and read the blob the shutdown was still in the middle of replacing. The process then held **two** `Room` objects for one world, both writing the same row through an `UPDATE` with no version guard: last write wins, and the eviction's is typically the older one, so the evicted room's final state — the last minutes before it emptied — silently lost. Eviction now hands the room from "live" to "closing" in one step: it leaves the registry (nobody may join a room that's closing its sockets) and a load for that world waits for the shutdown's write to land before reading the row, so it can only ever build a room from post-shutdown state.

content.content: 24:- **Renaming a cloud world no longer silently switches off cloud sync on your other devices** (⚠ adds migration `0004`; web + game server must deploy together): `worlds.updatedAt` was doing two unrelated jobs — metadata mtime (what the world list sorts by) and the save revision every device compares to decide whether the cloud moved. Renaming a world bumped it, so every _other_ device's sync cursor went stale over a save that hadn't changed by a single byte. Their next push came back **409 conflict**, and since a conflict latches sync off for the session to avoid clobbering another device, the result was a world that quietly stopped syncing until you noticed. No concurrency needed — one rename did it. The two jobs are now two columns: `updatedAt` stays metadata mtime, while the new monotonic `saveRevision` counts **blob writes and nothing else**, incremented SQL-side by both writers (the browser upload and the game server's room persistence) so concurrent writes can't settle on a stale read. Revision 0 means never saved, which is what lets the server accept a "first upload" without taking the client's word for it. Devices now store revisions (`minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2`), and because revisions are _ordered_ where timestamps were only compared for equality, the open-time reconcile asks whether the cloud is strictly **ahead** of your cursor rather than merely different — so a remote that's behind (a restored backup, a stale replica) can no longer overwrite newer local progress. The migration backfills existing worlds that already hold a blob to revision 1, since 0 would advertise them as never-saved. Also hardens the upload's base check: an unparseable revision is now rejected rather than quietly read as a first upload, which would have handed a stale client a clobber.

Revision 0 means never saved, which is what lets the server accept a "first upload" without taking the client's word for it. Devices now store revisions (`minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2`), and because revisions are _ordered_ where timestamps were only compared for equality, the open-time reconcile asks whether the cloud is strictly **ahead** of your cursor rather than merely different — so a remote that's behind (a restored backup, a stale replica) can no longer overwrite newer local progress. The migration backfills existing worlds that already hold a blob to revision 1, since 0 would advertise them as never-saved. Also hardens the upload's base check: an unparseable revision is now rejected rather than quietly read as a first upload, which would have handed a stale client a clobber.

+- **Renaming a cloud world no longer silently switches off cloud sync on your other devices** (⚠ adds migrations `0004`+`0005`): `worlds.updatedAt` was doing two unrelated jobs — metadata mtime (what the world list sorts by) and the save revision every device compares to decide whether the cloud moved. Renaming a world bumped it, so every _other_ device's sync cursor went stale over a save that hadn't changed by a single byte. Their next push came back **409 conflict**, and since a conflict latches sync off for the session to avoid clobbering another device, the result was a world that quietly stopped syncing until you noticed. No concurrency needed — one rename did it. The two jobs are now two columns: `updatedAt` stays metadata mtime, while the new monotonic `saveRevision` counts **blob writes and nothing else**. A **database trigger** (`0005`) owns the increment — it bumps `save_revision` on any UPDATE where `save_blob` actually changes — so every writer (the browser upload, the game server, even a mismatched build mid-deploy) advances it correctly, a rename structurally never does, and the web and game-server deploys **no longer have to ship from the same SHA** for this column. Revision 0 means never saved, which is what lets the server accept a "first upload" without taking the client's word for it. Devices now store revisions (`minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2`), and because revisions are _ordered_ where timestamps were only compared for equality, the open-time reconcile asks whether the cloud is strictly **ahead** of your cursor rather than merely different — so a remote that's behind (a restored backup, a stale replica) can no longer overwrite newer local progress. On an app upgrade a device that had synced under the old scheme has no revision cursor yet; rather than treat that as a first download and adopt (which would overwrite unsynced local progress), it keeps its local save and seeds the cursor from the current cloud revision, so any real cross-device conflict routes through the normal 409-and-warn path. `0004` backfills existing worlds that already hold a blob to revision 1, since 0 would advertise them as never-saved. Also hardens the upload's base check: an unparseable revision is rejected rather than quietly read as a first upload.

- **A malformed save is now refused at the door instead of crashing the engine**: `parseSave` — the one seam every save reader shares — documented itself as _total_ ("unknown shapes … all yield null") but only checked that the top-level `changes` and `players` were **arrays**, never what was in them. So a current-version save like `{version: 18, seed: 1, changes: [1], players: [null]}` passed validation and then threw deeper in, where nothing is defensive by design: the engine's constructor does `save.players.find((p) => p.id === …)` on the null, and `applySavedChanges` destructures every change as a tuple. It now validates entries — player entries must be objects with a string id, changes must be `[index, blockId]` integer pairs, and a `dimensions` section must carry a usable `changes` array. Malformed **entries drop** (one bad pair must not cost you your world — matching every other reader in the module, which has always dropped rather than thrown), while a malformed **save** still reads as no save. Block ids are bounded to the voxel array's 0–255 storage width, since a larger id wouldn't fail loudly — it would wrap (`300 & 255` = 44) and silently become a _different real block_ — but they're deliberately not allow-listed against `BlockId`, because a hand-maintained ceiling would silently discard legitimate blocks the day someone appends an id and forgets to raise it, trading a cosmetic failure (unknown ids already render magenta) for real data loss. Deep per-field validation stays where it already lives, in the restorers. Separately, the **cloud download** was the one save path that skipped all of this — it cast the decompressed JSON straight to `SaveData`, so a corrupt blob rode into the engine — and now validates like the rest; anything that isn't a save reads as "no save here", which the callers already treat as "keep what's local".

- **An invited player can no longer overwrite a multiplayer world's authoritative save**: `sp-cloud` and `mp` worlds keep their save in the same `worlds.saveBlob` column, but they don't share its ownership — an `sp-cloud` blob **is** the client's upload, while an `mp` blob is the game server's authoritative persistence, which a room reloads as world state on its next boot. `PUT /api/worlds/:id/save` gated on membership but never on `kind`, so anyone holding an invite could upload a crafted `SaveData` over a shared world and have the server adopt it wholesale on the next room boot — inventories, builds, the lot — bypassing the server authority the protocol reserves for itself ("clients cannot invent items or edits", [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md#trust-model)). Reads stay membership-gated: a member can already see the world by playing it. 1	# Deploying online multiplayer
2	
3	A first-time deploy runbook for the online stack. **Single-player needs none of
4	this** — it runs entirely in the browser, saving worlds to IndexedDB, and never
5	touches the network. Only online co-op (accounts, cloud saves, shared worlds) needs
6	a server; this page is how to stand that up.
7	
8	For _how the stack fits together_ see [online.md](online.md); for _operating_ a
9	running deployment (kick, revoke, replay, redeploys, capacity) see the
10	[ops runbook](online.md#runbook).
11	
12	## The shape of it
13	
14	Three managed pieces, sharing a database and one secret:
15	
16	```
17	        Vercel (Next app + better-auth + /api)  ─┐
18	Browser ┤                                         ├─ Neon Postgres (accounts, worlds, saves)
19	        └ Fly.io (Bun game server, WebSocket) ───┘
20	                    ▲
21	        share the SAME DATABASE_URL and a byte-identical GAME_TICKET_SECRET
22	```
23	
24	- **Vercel** hosts the Next.js app: menus, better-auth, and the `/api` routes
25	  (worlds, invites, cloud saves, join tickets).
26	- **Neon** (or any Postgres) holds accounts, world rows, memberships, invites,
27	  and gzipped save blobs.
28	- **Fly.io** runs the authoritative Bun game server (`server/`) — the long-lived
29	  WebSocket world rooms. It's on Fly and **not** Vercel because serverless
30	  functions can't hold persistent WebSockets; that split is deliberate.
31	
32	The only runtime link between Vercel and Fly is the **join ticket**: the web API
33	mints a 60-second HS256 token, the game server verifies it with the shared
34	`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`. They never call each other directly.
35	
36	## Prerequisites
37	
38	- Accounts on [Vercel](https://vercel.com), [Neon](https://neon.tech) (or another
39	  Postgres provider), and [Fly.io](https://fly.io).
40	- The [Fly CLI](https://fly.io/docs/flyctl/install/) (`fly`) and optionally the
41	  [Vercel CLI](https://vercel.com/docs/cli) (`vercel`).
42	- `bun` locally (to run the one migration).
43	
44	## Secrets to generate up front
45	
46	Generate these once and keep them handy — several are shared:
47	
48	```bash
49	openssl rand -base64 32   # BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (web only)
50	openssl rand -base64 32   # GAME_TICKET_SECRET (web AND game server — must match)
51	openssl rand -base64 24   # ADMIN_TOKEN (game server only; guards /rooms* admin endpoints)
52	```
53	
54	> **The #1 misconfiguration:** if `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` differs between Vercel and
55	> Fly, _every_ join fails with WebSocket close code **4000** (bad ticket). Set the
56	> exact same value in both.
57	
58	## Step 1 — Database (Neon)
59	
60	1. Create a Neon project and copy its pooled connection string (it looks like
61	   `REDACTED`). This is `DATABASE_URL`.
62	2. Apply the schema (runs the committed `db/migrations/0000_online-foundation.sql`):
63	
64	   ```bash
65	   DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' bun run db:migrate
66	   ```
67	
68	   Migrations are generated from `db/schema.ts` and committed under
69	   `db/migrations/`; `bun run db:migrate` (drizzle-kit) is the only step that
70	   needs a live database. Re-run it after any future schema change lands.
71	
72	## Step 2 — Game server (Fly.io)
73	
74	Run from the **repo root**. The commands are also in `server/fly.toml`'s header.
75	
76	```bash
77	fly launch --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile --no-deploy
78	fly secrets set \
79	  DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' \
80	  GAME_TICKET_SECRET='…the shared secret…' \
81	  ADMIN_TOKEN='…admin token…' \
82	  --config server/fly.toml
83	fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile
84	fly scale count 1 --config server/fly.toml
85	```
86	
87	The `fly scale count 1` is **not optional**: `fly launch` provisions a
88	two-machine HA pair by default, but rooms live in one process's memory
89	(`server/roomRegistry.ts` — no cross-instance coordination), so the app must run
90	**exactly one machine**. With two, Fly's edge load-balances each WebSocket
91	independently and players in the same world get split across two independent
92	copies of the room — everyone connects "successfully" and everyone is alone
93	(see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)). Confirm with
94	`fly machine list --config server/fly.toml` → exactly one machine.
95	
96	`server/fly.toml` already pins the rest of the important bits: a single region
97	(set `primary_region` by **measured** RTT, not by the map — it can't pin the machine
98	_count_, which is runtime state, hence the explicit scale step), **always
99	on** (`min_machines_running = 1`, `auto_stop_machines = "off"` — a room must keep
100	ticking while players are in it), a `/health` check, `PERSISTENCE = "postgres"`,
101	`MAX_ROOMS = 3`, and a 512 MB VM — rooms are ~74 MB each, so memory and
102	`MAX_ROOMS` scale **together** (6 rooms needs ~1 GB; resize with
103	`fly scale memory`, then raise the env). SIGTERM on a redeploy
104	drains every room to Postgres first, so a deploy loses at most the last 60 s
105	(the dirty-persist interval), crash-safe.
106	
107	**Region is `ord`, chosen by measurement.** For a mixed NA/Asia group, `sjc`
108	looked closer to Asia on the map but measured 3–10× worse in production
109	(Asia ~2000 ms & NA ~200 ms on `sjc`, vs Asia ~1000 ms & NA ~60 ms on `ord`) —
110	Fly's routing/peering to `sjc` is poor for these players' ISPs. Base latency
111	lives in the network path, not the server (an idle `/health` already round-trips
112	~260 ms), and the `ping` handler replies synchronously, so the client's F3
113	`rttMs` is a true RTT. Before changing region, read F3 `rttMs` from a real
114	client in each region you serve and let the numbers decide; don't pick by
115	geography. (A bigger VM does not help network RTT.)
116	
117	The app name in `fly.toml` is `monecraft-server`, so its URL is
118	`https://monecraft-server.fly.dev` — the browser connects over **`wss://`**
119	(`force_https` is on). Rename the app if you like, but then update the web app's
120	`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` to match.
121	
122	Confirm it's up:
123	
124	```bash
125	curl https://monecraft-server.fly.dev/health   # → {"ok":true,"rooms":0}
126	```
127	
128	## Step 3 — Web app (Vercel)
129	
130	Import the repo in the Vercel dashboard (or `vercel --prod` from the repo root),
131	then set these environment variables (see `.env.example` for the full list):
132	
133	| Variable                      | Value                                                   |
134	| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
135	| `DATABASE_URL`                | the **same** Neon string as the game server             |
136	| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`          | your `openssl rand` output                              |
137	| `BETTER_AUTH_URL`             | the deployed origin, e.g. `https://mc.ainaive.com`      |
138	| `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`          | the **same** shared secret as the game server           |
139	| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` | `wss://monecraft-server.fly.dev` (note **wss**, not ws) |
140	
141	`next build` won't _fail_ on a missing var (the auth mount and DB connection are
142	both lazy — a missing server-side var surfaces at runtime instead). But
143	`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` is the exception: it's **inlined into the client
144	bundle at build time**, so it must be set in the Vercel project **before** the
145	build runs, or online play ships pointing at nothing (single-player still works).
146	Set all five in Vercel before the first deploy, then double-check them.
147	
148	> **Ordering / chicken-and-egg:** `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is your Vercel origin and
149	> `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` is your Fly origin, so each side wants the other's
150	> URL. Both hostnames are predictable (`<project>.vercel.app`,
151	> `<app>.fly.dev`), so set them up front. If you use a custom domain, set the env
152	> var to the final URL and redeploy the web app once DNS is live. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`
153	> vars are inlined at build time — changing one needs a **redeploy**, not just an
154	> env edit.
155	
156	### Custom domain

+- **Renaming a cloud world no longer silently switches off cloud sync on your other devices** (⚠ adds migrations `0004`+`0005`): `worlds.updatedAt` was doing two unrelated jobs — metadata mtime (what the world list sorts by) and the save revision every device compares to decide whether the cloud moved. Renaming a world bumped it, so every _other_ device's sync cursor went stale over a save that hadn't changed by a single byte. Their next push came back **409 conflict**, and since a conflict latches sync off for the session to avoid clobbering another device, the result was a world that quietly stopped syncing until you noticed. No concurrency needed — one rename did it. The two jobs are now two columns: `updatedAt` stays metadata mtime, while the new monotonic `saveRevision` counts **blob writes and nothing else**. A **database trigger** (`0005`) owns the increment — it bumps `save_revision` on any UPDATE where `save_blob` actually changes — so every writer (the browser upload, the game server, even a mismatched build mid-deploy) advances it correctly, a rename structurally never does, and the web and game-server deploys **no longer have to ship from the same SHA** for this column. Revision 0 means never saved, which is what lets the server accept a "first upload" without taking the client's word for it. Devices now store revisions (`minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2`), and because revisions are _ordered_ where timestamps were only compared for equality, the open-time reconcile asks whether the cloud is strictly **ahead** of your cursor rather than merely different — so a remote that's behind (a restored backup, a stale replica) can no longer overwrite newer local progress. On an app upgrade a device that had synced under the old scheme has no revision cursor yet; rather than treat that as a first download and adopt (which would overwrite unsynced local progress), it keeps its local save when one exists and seeds the cursor from the current cloud revision, so any real cross-device conflict routes through the normal 409-and-warn path. `0004` backfills existing worlds that already hold a blob to revision 1, since 0 would advertise them as never-saved. Also hardens the upload's base check: an unparseable revision is rejected rather than quietly read as a first upload.

- **A malformed save is now refused at the door instead of crashing the engine**: `parseSave` — the one seam every save reader shares — documented itself as _total_ ("unknown shapes … all yield null") but only checked that the top-level `changes` and `players` were **arrays**, never what was in them. So a current-version save like `{version: 18, seed: 1, changes: [1], players: [null]}` passed validation and then threw deeper in, where nothing is defensive by design: the engine's constructor does `save.players.find((p) => p.id === …)` on the null, and `applySavedChanges` destructures every change as a tuple. It now validates entries — player entries must be objects with a string id, changes must be `[index, blockId]` integer pairs, and a `dimensions` section must carry a usable `changes` array. Malformed **entries drop** (one bad pair must not cost you your world — matching every other reader in the module, which has always dropped rather than thrown), while a malformed **save** still reads as no save. Block ids are bounded to the voxel array's 0–255 storage width, since a larger id wouldn't fail loudly — it would wrap (`300 & 255` = 44) and silently become a _different real block_ — but they're deliberately not allow-listed against `BlockId`, because a hand-maintained ceiling would silently discard legitimate blocks the day someone appends an id and forgets to raise it, trading a cosmetic failure (unknown ids already render magenta) for real data loss. Deep per-field validation stays where it already lives, in the restorers. Separately, the **cloud download** was the one save path that skipped all of this — it cast the decompressed JSON straight to `SaveData`, so a corrupt blob rode into the engine — and now validates like the rest; anything that isn't a save reads as "no save here", which the callers already treat as "keep what's local".

- **An invited player can no longer overwrite a multiplayer world's authoritative save**: `sp-cloud` and `mp` worlds keep their save in the same `worlds.saveBlob` column, but they don't share its ownership — an `sp-cloud` blob **is** the client's upload, while an `mp` blob is the game server's authoritative persistence, which a room reloads as world state on its next boot. `PUT /api/worlds/:id/save` gated on membership but never on `kind`, so anyone holding an invite could upload a crafted `SaveData` over a shared world and have the server adopt it wholesale on the next room boot — inventories, builds, the lot — bypassing the server authority the protocol reserves for itself ("clients cannot invent items or edits", [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md#trust-model)). Nothing legitimate ever uploaded an `mp` world (the in-game push returns early when online, and mp worlds carry no `cloudId`), so uploads are now `sp-cloud`-only — the mirror image of the `mp`-only check the join-ticket path already made. Reads stay membership-gated: a member can already see the world by playing it. Separately, the upload route now rejects an oversized body on its declared `content-length` before buffering it, and stored blobs inflate through a bounded gunzip (gzip runs ~1000:1 on hostile input, so an unbounded inflate turns a few MiB of stored bytes into GiB of heap on a 512 MB VM) — with the kind gate in place a room should only ever read blobs it wrote itself, so that bound is defense in depth rather than a live vector, but it's the seam where stored bytes become engine state and shouldn't trust the row on the far side.

- **Docs: corrected stale "client-only / localStorage / `Math.sin`" claims**: five pages still described the pre-online, pre-IndexedDB game. `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `docs/deploy.md` called the project single-player and client-only saving to localStorage — it has had an authoritative Bun game server, Postgres, accounts, and IndexedDB saves for several releases; `docs/manual.md` told **players** their worlds autosave to `localStorage`, contradicting its own earlier line (saves moved to IndexedDB in 0.15.0). `docs/save-format.md` still carried the retired "the noise functions use `Math.sin` … the tests prove refactor purity on the pinned Bun version, not cross-browser save portability" caveat — contradicting its own v11 entry, `docs/testing.md`, and `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`, which proves exactly the portability that caveat denied.
