lines: - **Backgrounding the game on a phone no longer switches off its own cloud sync**: six places push a cloud-linked world's save (autosave, three unload listeners, hardcore game-over, unmount, manual save) and several fire at once — backgrounding a mobile tab raises **both** `visibilitychange` and `pagehide`. Each fired its own upload immediately, so two pushes went out carrying the same base revision; the server accepted one and 409'd the other, and a 409 latches syncing off for the session to avoid clobbering another device. The result: a single device switched off its own cloud sync by conflicting with **itself**, and the toast blamed a device that didn't exist. Uploads now go through a latest-wins queue — one in flight, the newest snapshot behind it, superseded snapshots dropped (they describe the same world). The snapshot is taken when a push is _requested_ rather than when it runs, so the unload flush still uploads the state as of the unload. Separately, the open-time reconcile advanced this device's sync cursor _before_ the downloaded save was stored locally: if that write failed, the device claimed a save it didn't have and every later open read the cloud as "not ahead" and declined to adopt it — stranding the cloud save on that device permanently. The cursor now moves only once the local write has durably committed.

- **Renaming a cloud world no longer silently switches off cloud sync on your other devices** (⚠ adds migrations `0004`+`0005`): `worlds.updatedAt` was doing two unrelated jobs — metadata mtime (what the world list sorts by) and the save revision every device compares to decide whether the cloud moved. Renaming a world bumped it, so every _other_ device's sync cursor went stale over a save that hadn't changed by a single byte. Their next push came back **409 conflict**, and since a conflict latches sync off for the session to avoid clobbering another device, the result was a world that quietly stopped syncing until you noticed. No concurrency needed — one rename did it. The two jobs are now two columns: `updatedAt` stays metadata mtime, while the new monotonic `saveRevision` counts **blob writes and nothing else**. A **database trigger** (`0005`) owns the increment — it bumps `save_revision` on any UPDATE where `save_blob` actually changes — so every writer (the browser upload, the game server, even a mismatched build mid-deploy) advances it correctly, a rename structurally never does, and the web and game-server deploys **no longer have to ship from the same SHA** for this column. Revision 0 means never saved, which is what lets the server accept a "first upload" without taking the client's word for it. Devices now store revisions (`minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2`), and because revisions are _ordered_ where timestamps were only compared for equality, the open-time reconcile asks whether the cloud is strictly **ahead** of your cursor rather than merely different — so a remote that's behind (a restored backup, a stale replica) can no longer overwrite newer local progress. On an app upgrade a device that had synced under the old scheme has no revision cursor yet; rather than treat that as a first download and adopt (which would overwrite unsynced local progress), it keeps its local save when one exists and seeds the cursor from the current cloud revision, so any real cross-device conflict routes through the normal 409-and-warn path. `0004` backfills existing worlds that already hold a blob to revision 1, since 0 would advertise them as never-saved. lines: ### Fixed

- **Invite acceptance is now transactional, and resync requests are rate-limited**: two smaller online-server fixes. Accepting an invite consumed a use and then inserted the membership as two separate statements, so a failed insert burned a use with nothing to show for it, and two accepts from the _same_ user racing each other both passed a read-side "already a member?" check and each consumed a use — leaving two uses spent for the one membership the unique index actually created. The membership insert now goes first inside a transaction: concurrent same-user accepts dedupe on the index (the loser consumes nothing), and a use is spent if and only if a membership is granted. Separately, the `resync` message — which serializes and gzips a room's entire world diff — had no rate limit, so a hand-rolled client could loop it and stack full-world gzips against the 20 Hz tick loop every room in the process shares; it's now budgeted per second like the `cmd`/`chat`/`attack` messages. (No legitimate client sends `resync` in a loop; both are hardening against a crafted one.)

+- **Profile and world-rename endpoints validate their bodies too**: `createProfile`, `updateProfile`, and `renameWorld` took bare-cast JSON and called `.trim()` on the name, so a non-string name threw a `TypeError` (a 500 where a clean 400 belongs) — the same gap the world-creation fix closed, in the three sibling routes. They now type-check the name and validate `skinId` against the known skins (an unknown skin renders as the default anyway, so it isn't stored). Nothing legitimate changes.

+- **The game server drains in-flight work on shutdown**: `shutdownAll` (the SIGTERM/redeploy path) awaited only rooms already loaded, not a room still loading or one mid-eviction. So a load that finished just after shutdown began, or an eviction's final persist still running, could be skipped before `process.exit(0)` — losing that room's state on a deploy. It now refuses new loads and drains the loading and evicting sets before shutting down every resulting room, logging (not throwing on) any persist failure so one bad write can't strand the exit.

+- **Resetting a world can no longer resurrect the save it just deleted**: `resetNow` armed its unmount-save guard _after_ the async delete resolved, so an autosave tick or an unload flush firing during the delete window would rewrite the blob being removed. The guard is now armed _before_ the delete (and disarmed if the delete fails), mirroring the dimension-travel save that already documents exactly this ordering.

- **`POST /api/worlds` validates its body instead of trusting it**: the create-world handler cast the request JSON straight to its input type and passed it on, and the service checked only the name, kind, and that the seed was finite. So a hand-rolled request could set `worldType`/`gameMode`/`difficulty` to anything — the columns have no DB-level enum and the game server casts them straight into the engine at room boot — send a seed past int4 (a Postgres overflow surfaced as a 500, not a clean rejection), or set a non-string name that threw on `.trim()`. It now validates each field through the same `isWorldType`/`isGameMode`/`isDifficulty` guards the client already uses, bounds the seed to the column's range, and type-checks the rest. It also closes a **quota bypass**: `MAX_WORLDS_PER_PROFILE` was only checked when a `profileId` was supplied, so omitting it created uncapped, profile-less worlds — `mp` worlds (always profile-scoped in the UI) now require one, while `sp-cloud` stays account-level for the upload path. Nothing legitimate changes; the real client always sent valid values.

- **A brief network blip in an online world reconnects cleanly instead of sometimes killing the session**: the client's socket-close handling wasn't idempotent. A browser fires **both** `error` and `close` for an abnormal drop, and both ran the same close path — so one blip scheduled two reconnects, burned two rungs of the back-off ladder, minted two tickets, and raced two handshakes. The second handshake's join then kicked the first connection (`CLOSE_KICKED`, a fatal code), and because that orphaned socket's handlers were still bound, its close drove the session that had _just reconnected_ straight to "disconnected". A transient blip could therefore take down a session that had already recovered. Each socket now carries a connection generation: a close is acted on only for the live generation (a superseded socket's late close is ignored), and acting on one advances the generation so the same socket's error+close pair schedules exactly one reconnect. The reconnect timer is also single — a new rung clears any pending one rather than orphaning it. (Networking-only; no protocol or save change.)

- **Rejoining a world just as it's evicted can no longer resurrect it from stale state**: an idle room was dropped from the registry _before_ its shutdown finished persisting, and that final write is a whole-world gzip plus a Postgres round-trip — a window wide enough to land in. A join arriving inside it found no room, took the load path, and read the blob the shutdown was still in the middle of replacing. The process then held **two** `Room` objects for one world, both writing the same row through an `UPDATE` with no version guard: last write wins, and the eviction's is typically the older one, so the evicted room's final state — the last minutes before it emptied — silently lost. Eviction now hands the room from "live" to "closing" in one step: it leaves the registry (nobody may join a room that's closing its sockets) and a load for that world waits for the shutdown's write to land before reading the row, so it can only ever build a room from post-shutdown state.

fix: address round-2 review findings

Five app-level fixes from the re-review of this branch. (The sixth,
save_revision DB ownership, is the preceding commit — a schema change
kept separate.)

1. Cursor upgrade no longer overwrites newer local progress (data-loss
   regression from this branch's round 1). Round 1 moved the cloud sync
   cursor to a fresh localStorage key, so an upgraded device has no
   cursor and pullCloudSaveIfNewer treated that as a first download —
   adopting the (possibly older) cloud save over newer local progress.
   The absence of a cursor can't mean "first download" when a durable
   local save exists, so the reconcile now takes a hasLocalSave hint from
   the caller: no cursor + a local save keeps local and SEEDS the cursor
   from the current cloud revision (which also avoids a phantom
   first-upload 409 on the next push, since an empty base is rejected
   against an already-saved world); no cursor + no local still adopts
   (genuine fresh device / re-download). GameShell passes local-save
   existence via worldSaves.read.

2. Save-blob GET is sp-cloud-only, matching PUT. An mp blob is the whole
   authoritative world — every offline player's inventory/coords, both
   dimensions — so membership shouldn't buy a raw download of state a
   member never observed in-game. Nothing legitimate GETs an mp blob from
   the browser (the client pulls only sp-cloud; the game server reads via
   its own Postgres adapter), so the gate is free.

3. createProfile / updateProfile / renameWorld validate their bodies.
   They took bare-cast JSON and called .trim() on the name, throwing a
   TypeError (500) on a non-string — the same gap the round-1
   createWorld fix closed, in the three siblings. Now type-checked, with
   skinId validated against the known skins (isSkinId).

4. shutdownAll drains in-flight work. It awaited only rooms already in
   `rooms`, not a room still loading or one mid-eviction — so a load
   finishing just after shutdown began, or an eviction's final persist,
   could be skipped before process.exit(0). It now refuses new loads
   (shuttingDown) and drains the loading and evicting sets before
   shutting down every resulting room, logging rather than throwing on a
   failed persist. sweepIdle bails once shutting down so the drain has a
   fixed set.

5. resetNow arms the unmount-save guard BEFORE the async delete, not
   after — an autosave/flush in the delete window would otherwise rewrite
   the just-deleted blob. Disarms on failure. Mirrors the dimension-travel
   save, which already documents this exact ordering.

Regression tests for 1-4 (the reset fix is a read-verified ordering
change in the hook, which has no test harness). Full gate green: 1549
unit, build, lint, typecheck, format.
EOF

content.text:
Done. Round 2 is on PR #65 (2 commits, 15 total), gate fully green, and a summary comment posted for the reviewer.

## What I did with the re-review

Codex's re-review was strong — I verified all seven findings and **fixed six**, deferring one with rationale. The most important thing it caught was a **data-loss regression I introduced in round 1**, and it was right.

**The regression (#1).** My round-1 decision to use a fresh `_v2` cursor key meant an upgraded device — one with a durable local save but no cursor yet — got treated as a first download and *overwrote its newer local progress with the older cloud copy*. My own commit comment ("starting empty costs nothing") was simply wrong: the pull adopts before it sets the cursor. Fixed by discriminating on whether a local save exists, and seeding the cursor instead of overwriting.

**The best structural fix (#2).** Rather than document a fragile same-SHA deploy window, the `save_revision` increment now lives in a DB trigger. That's better than what I shipped in round 1: any writer bumps it correctly, a rename structurally can't, and **the same-SHA deploy constraint I introduced is gone entirely**. The migration test drives *old-style* updates to prove the database owns it.

**One reversal worth flagging.** In round 1 I told you "GET stays membership-gated by design" and you approved blocking only PUT. Codex pushed back that an `mp` blob contains far more than a member observes in-game (offline players' inventories, both dimensions), and nothing legitimate GETs it from the browser. It was right — GET is now `sp-cloud`-only too.

Plus three cheaper correctness fixes: body validation on the three sibling endpoints, shutdown draining in-flight loads/evictions, and the reset guard-ordering carried from round 1's medium findings.

**Deferred, with reasons:** the decompression-ceiling tuning (#4 — the live server vector is already closed and I don't have measured save sizes to set a tighter bound safely), and the caps/perf items.

**Process note:** the full suite flaked once on the nether determinism test — passed in isolation and on rerun. A hash mismatch can't come from load and my changes are orthogonal to worldgen, so it's pre-existing test-isolation noise, not this branch. Everything else was green across the board: 1549 unit, 35 e2e, build, lint, typecheck, format.

The two commits are structured exactly as we discussed — the schema change (A) separate from the five app fixes (B).

content.text:
PR #65 is in a mergeable state — green gate, reviewed twice by Codex plus my own verification each round. So "what's next" is really your call on a few forks. Here's the honest landscape:

**1. Merge + deploy (yours to trigger — I won't do it unsolicited).**
When you're ready, the sequence is:
- Run `bun run db:migrate` against prod — applies **both** `0004` (the column + backfill) and `0005` (the trigger).
- Then deploy. Round 2 removed the same-SHA constraint, so web and Fly no longer have to go together *for revision correctness* — but the migration must land before or with the deploy, per the usual "migrate first" rule in `docs/deploy.md`.
- One nuance worth knowing: the PR still says "Review hardening…" and is squash-merged, so the 15-commit history collapses to one commit on `main`. The CHANGELOG entries are written to read as one release note.

**2. The one thing tests can't fully cover: a manual two-device pass on the cursor fix.**
Finding #1 was a data-loss bug about *app upgrades* — the exact scenario is "device synced under the old cursor scheme, made offline progress, upgraded, reopened." The unit tests pin the logic, but the real proof is loading a build with a `_v1` cursor and no `_v2` on a device with newer local progress and confirming it survives. I can't drive a browser in-session, so that's a you-check if you want certainty before shipping to real users.

**3. Deferred work, if you'd rather keep building than ship.**
- `#4` decompression ceiling — small tuning, low value (server vector already closed).
- Account-level `sp-cloud` / invite caps — a product decision on storage growth.
- **The whole-region remesh (P1 perf)** — the big latent item. Codex flagged it both rounds; it's the multi-session chunked-meshing rewrite I deferred behind a real measurement. If you want to tackle something substantial next, this is it — but step one is *measuring* the actual remesh cost in a live frame, not assuming the 478ms.

My recommendation: **merge and deploy #65 first** (it fixes real data-loss bugs that are worth getting to users), do the two-device sanity check if you want belt-and-braces, then decide between the perf work and something new.

Want me to do anything concrete now — draft the merge/deploy steps as a checklist, start measuring the remesh cost, or something else?

_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Separate local single-player from account-backed `sp-cloud` single-player.**

Several docs imply that single-player is always local and that accounts/cloud saves belong only to co-op, but account mode supports client-side single-player worlds whose saves synchronize through the cloud.
- `AGENTS.md#L7-L7`: qualify “single-player” as local and mention account-backed single-player saves.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md#L3-L3`: avoid presenting cloud saves as co-op-only.
- `docs/deploy.md#L4-L6`: distinguish no game-server requirement for local gameplay from web-service requirements for accounts/cloud saves.
- `docs/manual.md#L811-L818`: scope browser/device-bound wording to local worlds.

_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Make queued frames generation- and disposal-aware.**

The close callbacks carry `gen`, but `onmessage` discards it. An old socket’s binary frame can finish decompression after reconnection and apply a stale world sync—or set the disposed session back to `online`. Queue `{ gen, data }`, reject stale/disposed entries, and recheck `gen` after `await gunzipWorldSync(...)`.

Add regression coverage for reconnect/dispose while a binary frame is in flight.

# PR #65 — round 3: address CodeRabbit review

## Context

PR #65 got automated reviews. **Greptile produced nothing** (50-credit trial cap, both rounds).
**CodeRabbit posted 14 inline comments.** CI `verify` is green; `e2e`/deploy jobs skip on PRs.

I verified each comment against the branch. Several are genuine bugs **in my own round-1/round-2
work**; the rest split into cheap hardening, doc corrections my round-2 changes made stale, deferrals,
and nits. This round fixes the confirmed-real set on the **same branch** (updates PR #65).

## Triage of the 14 comments

**A — Real bugs (fix):**

- **#3 `db/ddl.ts:107` + migration `0005` — trigger needs an `ELSE` (Major).** The trigger only sets
  `NEW.save_revision` when `save_blob` changes; a metadata-only update carrying a caller-supplied
  `NEW.save_revision` would keep it. No app code does that today (rename sets only name/updatedAt), but
  `ELSE NEW.save_revision := OLD.save_revision` makes the invariant fully DB-owned. **`0005` isn't
  applied anywhere yet (PR unmerged), so amend it in place** rather than add `0006`.
- **#10 `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:295` — `onerror` masks a fatal close code (Major, mine).**
  `socket.onerror` calls `onSocketClosed(gen, 1006, …)`, consuming the generation; a fatal `close`
  (e.g. 4000/4003) that follows is then dropped as stale and the session **reconnects instead of
  closing**. Per the WebSocket spec an `error` is *always* followed by `close`, so `onerror` should be
  a no-op (or log only) and let `onclose` carry the real code. The generation guard on `onclose` still
  covers the superseded-socket case.
- **#9 `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts` inbound queue — not generation/dispose-aware (Major).** The queue
  enqueues frames without the generation; an old socket's binary frame finishing gunzip after a
  reconnect can apply a stale worldSync (or flip a disposed session back to `online`). Enqueue
  `{ gen, data }`, drop stale-gen/disposed entries, and re-check `gen`/`disposed` after the gunzip
  await. Bundle with #10 (same file/subsystem).
- **#13 `server/room.ts:848` — unhandled `persist()` rejection (Major, mine).** `void this.persist()`
  has no `.catch`; my round-1 change made occupied rooms persist every interval, so a DB outage spams
  unhandled rejections on the shared process. `storeOnce` already re-marks dirty for retry — just
  `.catch(err => console.error(…))`.

**B — Cheap hardening (fix):**

- **#2 `app/api/worlds/[id]/save/route.ts` — full-digit header parse.** `Number.parseInt("1junk")` = 1,
  so a prefixed `x-base-revision`/`x-save-version` is accepted as its prefix. Require `^\d+$` before
  parsing; keep null handling for absent/blank base. Low impact (client always sends clean values) but
  cheap.
- **#11 `lib/online/worldsService.ts:211` — validate `profileId` type.** The only `createWorld` field
  without a runtime guard: `0` reads as absent, a truthy object reaches the Drizzle predicate. Add a
  `typeof … === "string"` guard when present, mirroring the round-1 name/enum guards.

**C — Doc corrections my round-2 changes made stale (fix):**

- **#4 `db/migrations/0004_save-revision.sql:17`** still says web+game-server must ship together —
  obsolete once `0005`'s trigger lands. Rewrite to "apply `0004` and `0005` before rollout".
- **#5 `docs/online.md:122-123`** still says "reads stay membership-gated for both" — stale after the
  round-2 GET gate. Clarify: membership gates world access/metadata; raw save *downloads* are
  `sp-cloud`-only (and rename the "Save upload is `sp-cloud`-only" heading to cover both verbs).
- **#6/#7 `docs/testing.md:20,35`** — pre-existing incomplete Voxel-store sentence and an "uncculled"
  typo. Tiny; sweep up while here.

**D — Defer (with rationale), unchanged from prior rounds:**

- **#12 `server/persistence.ts` decompression ceiling (Major, heavy lift).** The re-review's #4, already
  deferred: the live server vector is closed (mp blobs are server-written only), and lowering the 96 MiB
  ceiling without measured real-save sizes risks rejecting a legitimate large build. The only cheap part
  — the test's arbitrary `> 16 MiB` assertion — can be reworded, but the rewrite stays deferred.
- **#1 `AGENTS.md:7` doc precision** (distinguish local vs account-backed single-player) — low value; the
  current text isn't wrong, just coarse.

**E — Real but heavier — DECISION NEEDED (see questions):**

- **#8 `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` — per-world cursor keys (Major).** Two tabs read-modify-write the shared
  `minecraft_cloud_stamps_v2` JSON blob and can clobber each other's entries; a dropped cursor makes the
  next push send an empty base → 409 → sync latches off. A concrete instance of the multi-tab issue I'd
  deferred as a category. Fix: store each world's cursor under its own key. Clean, but adds another
  storage-key scheme on top of the round-2 `_v2` change and interacts with the new `hasLocalSave` logic.
- **#14 `server/roomRegistry.ts:103` — failed eviction persist → stale reload (Major, heavy lift).** The
  `evicting` promise swallows `room.shutdown()` failures via `.catch(()=>{})`, so a failed final persist
  reads as a *successful* eviction and `getOrLoad` reloads the pre-eviction blob. An edge in my round-1
  handoff. The correct recovery (keep the room, block the world, or retry) is a real design choice — the
  riskiest item to get right, lowest probability (needs a DB failure mid-eviction + a concurrent join).

## The fixes (scope per the questions)

Commit shape mirrors round 2: schema-touching change (the `0005` `ELSE`) can ride with the other fixes
or stand alone — decided below. Each fix ships with a regression test where there's a testable seam
(the two NetworkSession bugs, the trigger `ELSE`, the header parse, the `profileId` guard; the doc and
`.catch` changes are verified by reading/gate).

Representative files: `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), `db/migrations/0005_*.sql` +
`db/ddl.ts` (+ `db/migrations.test.ts`), `server/room.ts` (+ `server/room.test.ts`),
`app/api/worlds/[id]/save/route.ts`, `lib/online/worldsService.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), and the doc files.

## Verification

Per fix: `bun run format` + `bun run lint`. Before pushing: the full gate — `lint`, `typecheck`,
`format:check`, `bun test`, `build`, and `test:e2e` (check `lsof -ti:3000` first). Then push to update
PR #65 and reply to the CodeRabbit threads (resolve fixed, note deferrals with rationale).

Targeted checks: the #10 regression (error-then-fatal-close → closed, not reconnecting), the #9
regression (a stale binary frame after reconnect is dropped), the `0005` `ELSE` via an old-style
metadata update in `db/migrations.test.ts`, and the header-parse/`profileId` guards in
`worldsService.test.ts`.

  `ELSE NEW.save_revision := OLD.save_revision` makes the invariant fully DB-owned. **`0005` isn't
  applied anywhere yet (PR unmerged), so amend it in place** rather than add `0006`.
- **#10 `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:295` — `onerror` masks a fatal close code (Major, mine).**
  `socket.onerror` calls `onSocketClosed(gen, 1006, …)`, consuming the generation; a fatal `close`
  (e.g. 4000/4003) that follows is then dropped as stale and the session **reconnects instead of
  closing**. Per the WebSocket spec an `error` is *always* followed by `close`, so `onerror` should be
  a no-op (or log only) and let `onclose` carry the real code. The generation guard on `onclose` still
  covers the superseded-socket case.
- **#9 `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts` inbound queue — not generation/dispose-aware (Major).** The queue
  enqueues frames without the generation; an old socket's binary frame finishing gunzip after a
  reconnect can apply a stale worldSync (or flip a disposed session back to `online`). Enqueue
  `{ gen, data }`, drop stale-gen/disposed entries, and re-check `gen`/`disposed` after the gunzip
  await. Bundle with #10 (same file/subsystem).
- **#13 `server/room.ts:848` — unhandled `persist()` rejection (Major, mine).** `void this.persist()`
  has no `.catch`; my round-1 change made occupied rooms persist every interval, so a DB outage spams
  unhandled rejections on the shared process. `storeOnce` already re-marks dirty for retry — just
  `.catch(err => console.error(…))`.

- **#2 `app/api/worlds/[id]/save/route.ts` — full-digit header parse.** `Number.parseInt("1junk")` = 1,
  so a prefixed `x-base-revision`/`x-save-version` is accepted as its prefix. Require `^\d+$` before
  parsing; keep null handling for absent/blank base. Low impact (client always sends clean values) but
  cheap.

  without a runtime guard: `0` reads as absent, a truthy object reaches the Drizzle predicate. Add a
  `typeof … === "string"` guard when present, mirroring the round-1 name/enum guards.

  round-2 GET gate. Clarify: membership gates world access/metadata; raw save *downloads* are
  `sp-cloud`-only (and rename the "Save upload is `sp-cloud`-only" heading to cover both verbs).
- **#6/#7 `docs/testing.md:20,35`** — pre-existing incomplete Voxel-store sentence and an "uncculled"
  typo. Tiny; sweep up while here.

**D — Defer (with rationale), unchanged from prior rounds:**

- **#12 `server/persistence.ts` decompression ceiling (Major, heavy lift).** The re-review's #4, already
  deferred: the live server vector is closed (mp blobs are server-written only), and lowering the 96 MiB

## Context

**CodeRabbit posted 14 inline comments.** CI `verify` is green; `e2e`/deploy jobs skip on PRs.

I verified each comment against the branch. Several are genuine bugs **in my own round-1/round-2
work**; the rest split into cheap hardening, doc corrections my round-2 changes made stale, deferrals,
and nits. This round fixes the confirmed-real set on the **same branch** (updates PR #65).

## Triage of the 14 comments

**A — Real bugs (fix):**

- **#3 `db/ddl.ts:107` + migration `0005` — trigger needs an `ELSE` (Major).** The trigger only sets
  `NEW.save_revision` when `save_blob` changes; a metadata-only update carrying a caller-supplied
  `NEW.save_revision` would keep it. No app code does that today (rename sets only name/updatedAt), but
  `ELSE NEW.save_revision := OLD.save_revision` makes the invariant fully DB-owned. **`0005` isn't
  applied anywhere yet (PR unmerged), so amend it in place** rather than add `0006`.
- **#10 `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:295` — `onerror` masks a fatal close code (Major, mine).**
  `socket.onerror` calls `onSocketClosed(gen, 1006, …)`, consuming the generation; a fatal `close`
  (e.g. 4000/4003) that follows is then dropped as stale and the session **reconnects instead of
  closing**. Per the WebSocket spec an `error` is *always* followed by `close`, so `onerror` should be
  a no-op (or log only) and let `onclose` carry the real code. The generation guard on `onclose` still
  covers the superseded-socket case.
- **#9 `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts` inbound queue — not generation/dispose-aware (Major).** The queue
  enqueues frames without the generation; an old socket's binary frame finishing gunzip after a
  reconnect can apply a stale worldSync (or flip a disposed session back to `online`). Enqueue
  `{ gen, data }`, drop stale-gen/disposed entries, and re-check `gen`/`disposed` after the gunzip
  await. Bundle with #10 (same file/subsystem).
- **#13 `server/room.ts:848` — unhandled `persist()` rejection (Major, mine).** `void this.persist()`
  has no `.catch`; my round-1 change made occupied rooms persist every interval, so a DB outage spams
  unhandled rejections on the shared process. `storeOnce` already re-marks dirty for retry — just
  `.catch(err => console.error(…))`.

**B — Cheap hardening (fix):**

- **#2 `app/api/worlds/[id]/save/route.ts` — full-digit header parse.** `Number.parseInt("1junk")` = 1,
  so a prefixed `x-base-revision`/`x-save-version` is accepted as its prefix. Require `^\d+$` before
  parsing; keep null handling for absent/blank base. Low impact (client always sends clean values) but
  cheap.
- **#11 `lib/online/worldsService.ts:211` — validate `profileId` type.** The only `createWorld` field
  without a runtime guard: `0` reads as absent, a truthy object reaches the Drizzle predicate. Add a
  `typeof … === "string"` guard when present, mirroring the round-1 name/enum guards.

**C — Doc corrections my round-2 changes made stale (fix):**

- **#4 `db/migrations/0004_save-revision.sql:17`** still says web+game-server must ship together —
  obsolete once `0005`'s trigger lands. Rewrite to "apply `0004` and `0005` before rollout".

  round-2 GET gate. Clarify: membership gates world access/metadata; raw save *downloads* are
  `sp-cloud`-only (and rename the "Save upload is `sp-cloud`-only" heading to cover both verbs).

  typo. Tiny; sweep up while here.

- **#12 `server/persistence.ts` decompression ceiling (Major, heavy lift).** The re-review's #4, already
  deferred: the live server vector is closed (mp blobs are server-written only), and lowering the 96 MiB
  ceiling without measured real-save sizes risks rejecting a legitimate large build. The only cheap part
  — the test's arbitrary `> 16 MiB` assertion — can be reworded, but the rewrite stays deferred.
- **#1 `AGENTS.md:7` doc precision** (distinguish local vs account-backed single-player) — low value; the
  current text isn't wrong, just coarse.

  reads as a *successful* eviction and `getOrLoad` reloads the pre-eviction blob. An edge in my round-1
  handoff. The correct recovery (keep the room, block the world, or retry) is a real design choice — the
  riskiest item to get right, lowest probability (needs a DB failure mid-eviction + a concurrent join).

**Out:** **#8** (multi-tab per-world cursor keys) and **#14** (failed-eviction stale reload) — both

## Verification

-- Make the database own the save_revision increment.
--
-- 0004 split the cursor out of updated_at, but left the +1 to application code
-- (putSaveBlob and the game server's storeWorld). That is not deploy-safe: after
-- 0004 runs, an OLD web build still serving would update save_blob WITHOUT
-- bumping save_revision, so another device sees an unchanged revision and misses
-- the write — and an old first-upload could leave save_blob non-null at revision
-- 0, which a new client then treats as "never saved" and overwrites.
--
-- A BEFORE UPDATE trigger moves the increment onto the row, so EVERY writer — new
-- build, old build mid-deploy, the game server — bumps it correctly, and the web
-- and game-server deploys no longer have to be same-SHA for this column. It also
-- makes the "rename does not bump" rule structural rather than by-omission: a
-- rename changes name/updated_at but not save_blob, so IS DISTINCT FROM is false
-- and the revision holds. IS DISTINCT FROM (not =) so a first upload
-- (NULL -> blob) counts as a change and bumps 0 -> 1.
CREATE FUNCTION bump_save_revision() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.save_blob IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.save_blob THEN
    NEW.save_revision := OLD.save_revision + 1;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER worlds_bump_save_revision
  BEFORE UPDATE ON "worlds"
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION bump_save_revision();

input.old_string:
**Save upload is `sp-cloud`-only.** Both kinds keep their blob in the same
`worlds.saveBlob` column, but they do not share its ownership: an `sp-cloud`
blob **is** the client's upload, while an `mp` blob is the game server's
authoritative persistence (`server/persistence.ts`), which a room reloads as
world state on its next boot. So `putSaveBlob` gates on `kind` — otherwise
membership alone would let an invited player hand the room whatever world they
liked, bypassing the server authority [protocol.md](protocol.md#trust-model)
reserves ("clients cannot invent items or edits"). Nothing legitimate uploads an
`mp` world: `useMinecraftGame`'s push returns early when online, and mp worlds
carry no `cloudId`. `mintTicket` makes the mirror-image check (`mp` only), so
the two save paths stay disjoint. Reads stay membership-gated for both — a
member can already see the world by playing it.

world they liked, bypassing the server authority

edits"). `getSaveBlob` gates the same way: an `mp` blob is the whole
authoritative world (every offline player's inventory/coordinates, both

(never this route). `mintTicket` makes the mirror-image `mp`-only check, so the
two save paths stay disjoint.

14:- **The Nether works in online worlds (protocol v3→v4; save format v18 and worldgen 11 unchanged)**: light a portal in a co-op world and step through, exactly like single-player — and the party can split, with some players in the overworld and some in the Nether at once. The player list tags anyone who's "· Nether", a toast announces each crossing, and travel is seamless on the same connection (no reconnect). Server side, a room now runs an authoritative engine **per active dimension** ("dimension shards"): the overworld always, the nether born lazily on the first travel (or a rejoin whose save slice says nether) and persisted + dropped after `NETHER_SHARD_LINGER_MS` (60 s, env-tunable) once empty — and because the per-voxel light cache turns out to be renderer-only, **headless server engines now skip the light bake entirely (~40 MB and a full-world BFS saved per engine)**, so a two-shard room costs about what a one-engine room did before and the 512 MB Fly VM sizing is unchanged. Everything dimension-scoped got a real seam: tick channels and mob keyframes fan out per dimension (a cross-dimension keyframe would mass-prune a replica's mobs), the melee lag-comp history ring is per-shard, every pose/cmd carries a required dimension stamp (the travel race guard — frames in flight across a swap are dropped, never force-pose-fought), persistence composes both world halves at the room level, the day clock mirrors from the overworld (sleep counts only overworld players), and the owner's Peaceful despawns hostiles in every shard. The client rebuilds its replica engine and renderer in place around the live socket when the server says `dim`, prunes/adopts other players' avatars as they cross (`playerDim`), and a reconnect that raced a travel adopts the new dimension before resyncing. Deliberate scope: mobs (pets included) and vehicles stay behind — they are dimension state (your wolf waits by the portal); a mounted player can't accrue portal dwell at all (a raft drifting through a frame must never travel — this also fixes single-player); in-Nether deaths still respawn in the Nether. A new two-browser e2e drives the whole journey — a host builds and ignites a frame with real networked block placements, travels, is followed, and comes home — and [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md) now carries the version-bump rollout runbook this deploy will follow.
23:- **A brief network blip in an online world reconnects cleanly instead of sometimes killing the session**: the client's socket-close handling wasn't idempotent. A browser fires **both** `error` and `close` for an abnormal drop, and both ran the same close path — so one blip scheduled two reconnects, burned two rungs of the back-off ladder, minted two tickets, and raced two handshakes. The second handshake's join then kicked the first connection (`CLOSE_KICKED`, a fatal code), and because that orphaned socket's handlers were still bound, its close drove the session that had _just reconnected_ straight to "disconnected". A transient blip could therefore take down a session that had already recovered. Each socket now carries a connection generation: a close is acted on only for the live generation (a superseded socket's late close is ignored), and acting on one advances the generation so the same socket's error+close pair schedules exactly one reconnect. The reconnect timer is also single — a new rung clears any pending one rather than orphaning it. (Networking-only; no protocol or save change.)
25:- **A crashed game server no longer loses a session's progress that involved no block edit**: an online room persisted on its 60s interval only when a "dirty" flag was set — and exactly five things set it: dimension travel, a nether-shard evict, join, leave, and block-edit events. Everything else a live session does — inventory, health, hunger, status effects, XP, statistics, advancements, mob and container state, position — marked nothing. Mine nothing for twenty minutes while fighting, trading, brewing and levelling, and a hard crash (SIGKILL, an OOM, a Fly host fault) rolled all of it back; graceful paths were fine, since join/leave mark dirty and shutdown always persists, so this only ever showed up as a crash losing more than it should. An **occupied** room now persists on the interval regardless of the flag, which stays on only to decide whether an empty room still owes a write — chasing every mutation site would be a list to keep in sync forever, and one omission is a silent loss. Persistence also **coalesces**: it was fire-and-forget with no in-flight guard, so two stores could overlap on an unguarded `UPDATE` and land out of order, the older winning; and a store's completion could clear the dirty flag against an edit that arrived _during_ the write, swallowing it until the next unrelated block edit. Now one store runs at a time with at most one follow-up queued, the flag is cleared against the snapshot actually taken, and a failed write re-marks the room dirty to retry rather than dropping the state.
85:- **Smooth remote players/mobs on jittery connections — adaptive interpolation + hardened clock sync**: the interpolation delay (how far in the past remote entities render) is no longer a fixed 125 ms — it now sizes itself from measured tick-arrival jitter (125–450 ms, drifting at most 60 ms/s so nothing visibly warps). On a clean LAN nothing changes; on a jittery long-haul link remote players stop freeze-and-snapping. The server-clock estimate switches from a pure EWMA to an NTP-style min-RTT pick (the pong least inflated by queueing anchors the offset; slewed, snapping only on reconnect-sized jumps), and pings tighten from 2 s to 1 s to keep that window fresh.

content.content: 29:- **An invited player can no longer overwrite a multiplayer world's authoritative save**: `sp-cloud` and `mp` worlds keep their save in the same `worlds.saveBlob` column, but they don't share its ownership — an `sp-cloud` blob **is** the client's upload, while an `mp` blob is the game server's authoritative persistence, which a room reloads as world state on its next boot. `PUT /api/worlds/:id/save` gated on membership but never on `kind`, so anyone holding an invite could upload a crafted `SaveData` over a shared world and have the server adopt it wholesale on the next room boot — inventories, builds, the lot — bypassing the server authority the protocol reserves for itself ("clients cannot invent items or edits", [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md#trust-model)). Nothing legitimate ever uploaded an `mp` world (the in-game push returns early when online, and mp worlds carry no `cloudId`), so uploads are now `sp-cloud`-only — the mirror image of the `mp`-only check the join-ticket path already made. **Downloads (GET) are `sp-cloud`-only too**: an `mp` blob is the whole authoritative world — every (including offline) player's inventory, coordinates, health and both dimensions — which is far more than a member ever observes in-game, and nothing legitimate GETs it from the browser (the client only pulls `sp-cloud` cloud saves; the game server reads via its own Postgres adapter), so membership no longer buys a raw download of it. Separately, the upload route now rejects an oversized body on its declared `content-length` before buffering it, and stored blobs inflate through a bounded gunzip (gzip runs ~1000:1 on hostile input, so an unbounded inflate turns a few MiB of stored bytes into GiB of heap on a 512 MB VM) — with the kind gate in place a room should only ever read blobs it wrote itself, so that bound is defense in depth rather than a live vector, but it's the seam where stored bytes become engine state and shouldn't trust the row on the far side.

content.content: 39:- **Deflaked the simulated-latency FIFO (a real reorder, not a test artifact)**: the latency-simulation knob scheduled one `setTimeout` per delayed message, relying on the timer heap to fire equal-deadline timers in creation order — but that tie-breaking is not stable in Bun, and the monotonic delivery cursor _clamps_ every message behind a high jitter draw to the exact same deadline, making ties the common case. Result: rare genuine reordering of simulated-latency traffic (caught by the jitter-FIFO unit test going red on `main`, ~2/100 locally). Each direction now drains through a queued **delay line** — the same cursor, but one timer chain delivering in queue order, so FIFO comes from the queue rather than from timer tie-breaking; `dispose()` clears both lines, so no stray delivery timers outlive a session. Dev/testing code path only (simulated latency is never on in real play) — no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change — though the lagged multiplayer e2e steps (400±100 ms) inherit the stronger ordering guarantee.

lines: - **The game server drains in-flight work on shutdown**: `shutdownAll` (the SIGTERM/redeploy path) awaited only rooms already loaded, not a room still loading or one mid-eviction. So a load that finished just after shutdown began, or an eviction's final persist still running, could be skipped before `process.exit(0)` — losing that room's state on a deploy. It now refuses new loads and drains the loading and evicting sets before shutting down every resulting room, logging (not throwing on) any persist failure so one bad write can't strand the exit.

- **Resetting a world can no longer resurrect the save it just deleted**: `resetNow` armed its unmount-save guard _after_ the async delete resolved, so an autosave tick or an unload flush firing during the delete window would rewrite the blob being removed. The guard is now armed _before_ the delete (and disarmed if the delete fails), mirroring the dimension-travel save that already documents exactly this ordering.

- **`POST /api/worlds` validates its body instead of trusting it**: the create-world handler cast the request JSON straight to its input type and passed it on, and the service checked only the name, kind, and that the seed was finite. So a hand-rolled request could set `worldType`/`gameMode`/`difficulty` to anything — the columns have no DB-level enum and the game server casts them straight into the engine at room boot — send a seed past int4 (a Postgres overflow surfaced as a 500, not a clean rejection), or set a non-string name that threw on `.trim()`. It now validates each field through the same `isWorldType`/`isGameMode`/`isDifficulty` guards the client already uses, bounds the seed to the column's range, and type-checks the rest.
